summary:
I checked everything below against current source code and live chain state on 2026-10-08. Mainnet runs specVersion 475 (block about 9,240,300). The main branch of the source repo is at spec 476, one bump ahead. Both repos have moved. github.com/opentensor/subtensor now redirects to RaoFoundation/subtensor, which also holds the SDK, CLI and docs. opentensor/bittensor became RaoFoundation/bittensor and was archived on 2026-07-10. docs.learnbittensor.org returns a 301 redirect to bittensor.com/docs, which is built from the repo's /docs folder. The Python package on PyPI is bittensor 11.3.0, released 2026-10-07.

Much of the 2025 picture you may have is now out of date:
(1) **Pools.** Each subnet pool is a Balancer-style weighted pool (two reserves plus weights), not Uniswap-v3. User liquidity positions are permanently disabled. Every live pool currently sits at weights of about 0.5/0.5, so the swap math reduces to constant product (x*y=k). The swap fee is 33/65535 (about 0.05%) on the input side and goes to the block author.
(2) **Emission split across subnets.** It is no longer Taoflow. Since about 2026-06-23 (spec v431, the last flow-EMA update was at block 8,466,530) the split follows each subnet's price EMA, scaled by (1 − MinerBurned) and then passed through an "emission gate". The gate is a soft cutoff: subnets ranked roughly below 32nd by price share receive almost no TAO emission. I rebuilt the formula from source and it reproduces live per-subnet emissions to 5 decimals.
(3) **Halving.** The first TAO halving happened at block 7,103,975 (2025-12-15 13:31 UTC). Block emission is now 0.5 TAO, about 3,600 TAO/day. The next halving comes when total issuance reaches 15.75M (issuance is now 11.60M).
(4) **Faster price EMA.** On-chain SubnetMovingAlpha is 0.0003, 100 times the code default. A mature subnet's price EMA therefore has a half-life of only about 8 hours, so emission responds to price within hours.
(5) **Root Reborn (v441).** Root dividends are no longer sold every block. They accumulate as alpha in per-validator "baskets" and are sold only when stakers claim or validators trade.
(6) **Lifecycle values differ from the docs.** Subnet limit is 128, and all 128 slots are full. Immunity is 864,000 blocks (about 120 days). The minimum lock is 1 TAO, while the live registration cost is about 969 TAO. Registrations are limited to one per 14,400 blocks network-wide. Each new registration prunes the non-immune subnet with the lowest price EMA.

The biggest risk for a micro-cap strategy is deregistration. Holders are paid pro-rata from the pool's TAO reserve. The denominator includes the pool's own alpha and protocol-owned alpha, and validator basket holdings are sold through the pool first. The payout per alpha is typically 35–65% below the spot price.

A second structural point for micro-caps: tail subnets below the gate get almost no TAO injection and no protocol buybacks. They still mint 1 alpha per block to owner, miners and validators, so they face heavy dilution with nothing offsetting it.

findings.claim: Subnet pools are Balancer-style weighted pools, not Uniswap-v3. Concentrated or user liquidity is permanently disabled. Every live pool currently has weights of about 0.5/0.5, so the math is effectively constant product.
findings.detail: In pallets/swap/src/pallet/balancer.rs, x is the alpha reserve (SubnetAlphaIn), y is the TAO reserve (SubnetTAO), w1 is the base (alpha) weight and w2 the quote (TAO) weight, with w1 + w2 = 1. Only w2 is stored, as SwapBalancer[netuid].quote (a Perquintill with ACCURACY = 1e18). Both weights are bounded to at least MIN_WEIGHT = 0.01, which the source comment wrongly states as [0.1, 0.9]. Spot price is p = (w1/w2)*(y/x). The invariant is L = x^w1 * y^w2. The migration migrate_swapv3_to_balancer removed the V3 tick, position and fee storage. The add_liquidity, remove_liquidity, modify_position, toggle_user_liquidity and disable_lp calls now all return Error::Deprecated, with the note 'user liquidity is permanently disabled'. The docs page emissions.mdx still describes a per-subnet user_liquidity_enabled toggle; the code says otherwise. Live snapshot at block 9,240,299: all 128 pools have SwapBalancer quote weight about 0.5000. For example, SN92 spot from the runtime API is 0.001348212 and TAO/alpha_in is 587.2/435,539 = 0.0013482.

verification.evidence: balancer.rs: p=(w1/w2)(y/x), L=x^w1*y^w2, only quote weight stored as Perquintill, ACCURACY=1e18, MIN_WEIGHT=ACCURACY/100 while the header comment still says [0.1,0.9]. swap mod.rs: toggle_user_liquidity, add_liquidity, remove_liquidity, modify_position and disable_lp all return Error::Deprecated, with the note 'user liquidity is permanently disabled'. migrate_swapv3_to_balancer removes Ticks, Positions, FeeGlobal*, CurrentTick, EnabledUserLiquidity and related storage. docs/concepts/emissions.mdx still mentions a 'user_liquidity_enabled toggle'. Live at block 9,240,380: all 128 SwapBalancer entries are set, with quote weight between 0.49999974 and 0.5. SwapRuntimeApi_current_alpha_price(92) returned 1,348,210 (0.00134821). SN92 TAO/alpha_in = 587.199/435,539.5.

findings.claim: Exact swap output formulas to code (fee comes off the input first, then the weighted-pool formula is applied). I checked these against the on-chain sim_swap runtime API.
findings.detail:
BUY (TAO to alpha): fee = floor(tao_in * FeeRate / 65535). dy = tao_in - fee. alpha_out = x * (1 - (y/(y+dy))^(w2/w1)). With w1 = w2 = 0.5 this is alpha_out = x*dy/(y+dy). New reserves: y' = y + dy (the fee leaves the pool to the block author), x' = x - alpha_out.
SELL (alpha to TAO): fee_a = floor(alpha_in * FeeRate / 65535). dx = alpha_in - fee_a. tao_out = y * (1 - (x/(x+dx))^(w1/w2)). After that, the chain swaps fee_a alpha fee-free for TAO and pays the block author (settle_alpha_fee_to_author). So the pool absorbs the full alpha_in, and the user receives only tao_out.
Price-limit sizing: buying up to price p' needs dy = y*((p'/p)^w1 - 1); selling down to p' needs dx = x*((p/p')^w2 - 1). If the limit binds, the fee is recomputed as delta_in * rate/(65535 - rate).
Guards: the output reserve must be at least MinimumReserve = 1,000,000 rao before the swap (otherwise ReservesTooLow). The net input must be at most 1,000 times the input reserve (otherwise SwapInputTooLarge). Output cannot exceed the reserve (otherwise InsufficientLiquidity).
Verification: on SN92 at block 9,240,299, a 10 TAO buy gave tao_fee 0.005035477, net in 9.994964523 and alpha_out 7,289.41, matching x*dy/(y+dy). A 100 TAO buy into SN92 gave 63,351.6 alpha with 10,820.7 alpha of price impact (about 14.6%). The same 100 TAO into SN51 lost only 1.08 alpha to impact.

verification.evidence: swap_step.rs: fee = calculate_fee_amount, i.e. amount*(FeeRate/u16::MAX) truncated. Output: x*(1-(y/(y+dy))^(w2/w1)) for a buy and y*(1-(x/(x+dx))^(w1/w2)) for a sell. When the limit binds, the fee is recomputed as delta*rate/(65535-rate). impls.rs: ReservesTooLow if the output reserve is below MinimumReserve (runtime SwapMinimumReserve = 1,000,000). SwapInputTooLarge if net > 1000*input reserve (MAX_SWAP_INPUT_RESERVE_MULTIPLIER = 1_000). InsufficientLiquidity if paid_out > reserve. stake_utils.rs: on a buy, SubnetTAO += amount_paid_in (net) and settle_tao_fee_to_author moves the fee out. On a sell, SubnetAlphaIn += net, then settle_alpha_fee_to_author swaps the fee alpha fee-free (drop_fees=true) and pays the author. My own state_call at block 9,240,388: a 10 TAO buy on SN92 gave [9.994964523, 7289.425629, fee 0.005035477]; 100 TAO on SN92 gave 63,351.67 alpha with 10,820.70 slippage (14.6%); 100 TAO on SN51 gave 1.0827 slippage.

findings.claim: Swap fee is FeeRate/65535 on the input side. The default is 33 (about 0.0504%) and every live subnet uses it. 100% of the swap fee goes to the block author. Extrinsic transaction fees are separate and are recycled.
findings.detail:
DefaultFeeRate = 33. FeeRate is a per-netuid u16 map (Twox64Concat) that only root can set (set_fee_rate), capped at MaxFeeRate = 10,000 (about 15.26%). The live snapshot shows all 128 subnets at 33. A TAO-side fee is transferred to the block author. An alpha-side fee is first swapped fee-free for TAO, then sent to the author. If no author is known, the fee is burned.
Moves within one subnet between hotkeys involve no swap and no fee. A cross-subnet move runs two swaps but is charged the fee once.
Root (netuid 0) staking is 1:1 with no fee.
Protocol 'chain buys' (excess TAO swapped into alpha every block) run with drop_fees = true.
Extrinsic fee: a weight fee plus 1 rao per byte, paid in TAO and recycled (it reduces issuance) since v445. remove_stake-type calls can pay the fee in alpha, which is sold and recycled.
Minimum stake is DefaultMinStake = 2,000,000 rao (0.002 TAO) plus the fee.
NominatorMinRequiredStake on-chain is 0.01 TAO. After an unstake, a remaining nominator position worth less than that is force-unstaked.

verification.correction: Everything holds except NominatorMinRequiredStake. That storage item is a per-million factor of DefaultMinStake, not a rao amount. The on-chain raw value 10,000,000 means a factor of 10, so the nominator minimum is 2,000,000*10,000,000/1,000,000 = 20,000,000 rao = 0.02 TAO, not 0.01 TAO. The threshold is compared in alpha at spot (min_alpha = 0.02 TAO / spot). Positions below it are force-unstaked after remove_stake-type calls; the comment says 'no fees', but the code passes drop_fees=false.
verification.evidence: utils/misc.rs get_nominator_min_required_stake = DefaultMinStake * factor / 1_000_000; lib.rs comment says 'Factor of DefaultMinStake in per-mill format'. On-chain raw is 0x8096980000000000 = 10,000,000. Everything else checks out. DefaultFeeRate = 33; FeeRate is a Twox64Concat map; set_fee_rate requires ensure_root; runtime SwapMaxFeeRate = 10000. All 128 subnets have FeeRate 33 (unset, so default). transition_stake_internal sets drop_fee_origin = (origin is root) and drop_fee_destination = !drop_fee_origin, so a move is charged once. Root uses mechanism 0, so the fee is 0 and the swap is 1:1. Chain buys pass drop_fees=true. With no author, the fee is burned. The v445 release notes and transactions.mdx confirm that TAO fees are recycled and that alpha-paid fees are sold and recycled. SubtensorInitialMinStake = 2,000,000 rao, and validate_add_stake requires min_stake + fee.

findings.claim: Cross-subnet TAO emission is now based on each subnet's price EMA, scaled by (1 − MinerBurned), then passed through a soft cutoff (a Hill-function emission gate). It is not Taoflow.
findings.detail:
get_shares() in coinbase/subnet_emissions.rs works in four steps:
(1) Eligible subnets: non-root, FirstEmissionBlockNumber set, SubtokenEnabled, and NetworkRegistrationAllowed.
(2) s_i = SubnetMovingPrice_i / Σ SubnetMovingPrice.
(3) b_i = s_i*(1 - min(MinerBurned_i, 1)) / Σ(s*(1 - MB)). If every weight is zero, fall back to s.
(4) Gate: g_i = b_i / (1 + (theta/b_i)^h), then final_i = g_i / Σ g. If every g is zero, fall back to ungated shares.
Gate settings: h = EmissionGateExponent, default 3 (unset on-chain, so 3). theta = EmissionGateBar, recomputed when block % 360 == 0. In rank mode (EmissionBarRank N > 0), theta is the Nth-largest positive b. On-chain EmissionBarRank is unset, so the default N = 32 applies, and it overrides EmissionBarQuantile (stored as 0.75, unused). Live theta = 0.0082624; the 32nd-largest b computed from a live snapshot was 0.0082615.
Subnets with SubnetEmissionEnabled = false get zero TAO share, renormalized among enabled subnets: subnet_tao_i = 0.5 TAO * final_i / Σ_enabled final.
Check: this model reproduced SubnetTaoInEmission + SubnetExcessTao for every subnet to 5 decimals, and the actual emissions summed to 0.50000 TAO. Example: SN51, with EMA 0.0999, gets 13.09% (0.06545 TAO/block). A subnet with EMA about 0.0046 gets about 0.1%. Subnets with MinerBurned = 1 (for example SN95, EMA rank about 8) get 0 TAO.

verification.evidence: subnet_emissions.rs get_shares chains get_shares_price_ema, then scale_price_shares_by_miner_burn, then maybe_update_emission_gate_bar, then apply_emission_gate, where gate = 1/(1+(theta/s)^h). In rank mode theta is the Nth-largest positive share. It updates when block % 360 == 0, or when theta == 0. Eligibility comes from get_subnets_to_emit_to. Disabled subnets are zeroed and their share renormalized in get_subnet_block_emissions. On-chain: EmissionBarRank unset (default 32), EmissionGateExponent unset (default 3), EmissionBarQuantile stored as 0xc000.. = 0.75 (the code default is 0.61), EmissionGateBar = 0.0082624. My recomputation at block 9,240,382 matched SubnetTaoInEmission+SubnetExcessTao for all 125 eligible subnets to within 2.1e-7 TAO, with a total of 0.49999994. The 32nd-largest positive b was 0.0082620. SN51 gets 0.065467 TAO/block (13.09%). SN95 has MB = 1, EMA rank 8, and 0 emission.

findings.claim: History of the cross-subnet emission rule (needed if you backtest across regimes): price-based (Feb–Nov 2025) → Taoflow user-flow EMA (from about Nov 2025) → net TAO flow (May 2026) → price EMA (v431, about 2026-06-23) → emission gate (v440, July 2026) → miner-burn scaling removed in v444 (Aug 6) and restored in #3071 (Aug 12, 2026).
findings.detail:
The Taoflow code is still in subnet_emissions.rs, marked dead_code:
- Flow EMA per block: ema = (1 - a)*ema + a*block_flow, where a = FlowEmaSmoothingFactor / i64::MAX. The default 29,597,889,189,277 gives a ≈ 3.209e-6, a half-life of about 216,000 blocks (about 30 days).
- Net flow (May 2026) = user_ema - norm*protocol_ema, where norm = min(1, Σ user_ema⁺ / Σ protocol_ema⁺).
- Offset: z_i = max(S_i - L, 0), with L = max(TaoFlowCutoff, min(min_i S_i, 0)).
- Shares: z_i^p / Σ z^p, with p = FlowNormExponent, default 1.
On-chain, SubnetEmaTaoFlow was last updated at block 8,466,530 (2026-06-23T01:25Z per the archive node's timestamp). Raw SubnetTaoFlow accumulators keep growing but no longer feed emission. The SDK read subnet_tao_flows therefore returns stale EMAs.
Release notes describe v431 (July 2026) as 'Emission between subnets is now allocated purely in proportion to each subnet's moving-average price', with the root-proportion term removed from the cross-subnet split.
sources: archive node: SubnetEmaTaoFlow last_block field; Timestamp.Now at block 8,466,530

verification.correction:
The regime dates and labels are partly wrong.
(1) The flow-to-price switch was spec 421 at block 8,466,530 (2026-06-23 01:25Z), not v431.
(2) From 06-23 to 07-16 the share was price_EMA × root_proportion × (1 − MinerBurned), normalized with no gate. I verified this exactly at block 8,550,000 (L1 error 0.0; pure price gave 0.67). So miner-burn scaling began 2026-06-23, not with v440.
(3) The 'v431' release (on-chain spec 432) went live at block 8,636,190 (2026-07-16 19:30Z). It removed root_proportion from the cross-subnet split.
(4) v440 (the gate) went live at block 8,713,793 (2026-07-27 14:16Z).
(5) Spec 444 was never deployed on mainnet. Spec 443 (2026-08-04 18:37Z) ran until spec 445 at block 8,831,003 (2026-08-12 21:06Z). The miner-burn removal commit (Aug 6) therefore most likely never ran on-chain; the restore commit (#3071) merged 22 minutes before 445 went live.
(6) Also, at block 8,550,000, 64 of 128 subnets had SubnetEmissionEnabled = false.
The Taoflow formulas and the SubnetEmaTaoFlow freeze at 8,466,530 are correct.
verification.evidence: The archive node binary search gave spec 419 at 8,466,529, 421 at 8,466,530, 432 first at 8,636,190, 440 at 8,713,793, 441 at 8,765,683, 442 at 8,770,559, 443 at 8,772,666, and 445 at 8,831,003, with Timestamp.Now read at each block. Commit history of subnet_emissions.rs: c3841130 'Switch subnet emissions to price-based shares and root-proportion injection cap' (06-22), 5c1b3808 'Scale chain emission away from subnets burning miner emission' (06-22), eaadb745 'Weight emission shares by root_proportion' (06-22), bb3591e7 'remove root prop from emission calculation' (06-30), 791e9999 'release v440' (07-27), 1a587cc8 (08-06), d3f40e44 #3071 (08-12T20:44Z). Every SubnetEmaTaoFlow last_block equals 8,466,530. The flow code (FlowEmaSmoothingFactor 29,597,889,189,277/i64::MAX, lower limit, FlowNormExponent 1, net-flow normalization) matches.
sources: https://archive.chain.opentensor.ai (state_getRuntimeVersion and Timestamp.Now by block; storage at block 8,550,000)

findings.claim: The price EMA (SubnetMovingPrice) updates every block. Its warm-up depends on subnet age, and it takes the spot price capped at 1.0. On-chain SubnetMovingAlpha is 0.0003 (100 times the code default), which gives mature subnets a half-life of about 8 hours.
findings.detail:
update_moving_price, called every block after the coinbase for emitting subnets:
- a = SubnetMovingAlpha * b/(b + H), where b = current_block - (FirstEmissionBlockNumber - 1) and H = EMAPriceHalvingBlocks[netuid] (default 201,600 blocks, about 4 weeks; every subnet uses the default).
- ema' = a*min(spot, 1.0) + (1 - a)*ema.
The code default for SubnetMovingAlpha is 0.000003 (I96F32), with a comment about a 30-day 50% lag. On-chain it is 1,288,490/2^32 = 0.0003.
Resulting half-life: for a mature subnet (b ≈ 4M), a ≈ 2.86e-4, so about ln2/a ≈ 2,400 blocks ≈ 8 hours. For a subnet at b = H (4 weeks old), a = 1.5e-4, about 15 hours.
New or reused netuids start with EMA 0 (SubnetMovingPrice is removed on dissolve, and DefaultMovingPrice = 0). Observed: SN108, about 21k blocks after start-call, has EMA 0.0039 against spot 0.0122. SN116 has 0.0175 against 0.0347.
A separate fast EMA, SubnetFastMovingPrice (half-life 600 blocks, uncapped), is used only for basket-trading price bands.
The moving price drives three things: emission shares, the root-sell flag (Σ EMA > 1) and pruning.
sources: mainnet storage SubtensorModule.SubnetMovingAlpha = 0x...13a92a (1288490) and SubnetMovingPrice per netuid

verification.evidence: stake_utils.rs update_moving_price: alpha = SubnetMovingAlpha*b/(b+H), with b = now − (FirstEmissionBlockNumber − 1); ema' = alpha*min(spot,1) + (1 − alpha)*ema. DefaultMovingAlpha = 0.000003 (comment: '30 days to reach 50%'). On-chain SubnetMovingAlpha raw is 1,288,490/2^32 = 0.0003. EMAPriceHalvingBlocks is 201,600 for every subnet. block_step runs update_moving_prices after run_coinbase, for emitting subnets only. SubnetMovingPrice is removed on dissolve and DefaultMovingPrice = 0. BASKET_FAST_EMA_HALF_LIFE_BLOCKS = 600, uncapped. Live: SN108 EMA 0.00395 vs spot 0.01221; SN116 EMA 0.0175 vs spot 0.0347. Minor addition: the slow EMA is also one of the references for the swap_basket 2% band.

findings.claim: Per-block injection: tao_in and alpha_in are added at spot price by adjusting the pool weights, so injection does not move price. TAO that cannot be injected (because of the root-proportion cap) is used to buy alpha in the subnet's pool ('chain buys'), and that alpha becomes protocol-owned.
findings.detail:
get_subnet_terms, using the subnet's TAO emission E_i:
- price_i = current spot price.
- alpha_in = E_i/price_i.
- cap = root_proportion_i * alpha_emission_i. If alpha_in > cap, then alpha_in = cap and tao_in = cap*price_i; otherwise tao_in = E_i.
- excess = E_i - tao_in.
- root_proportion_i = (SubnetTAO[0]*TaoWeight) / (SubnetTAO[0]*TaoWeight + alpha_issuance_i).
The excess is swapped TAO→alpha with no fee and no price limit, and the bought alpha accrues to SubnetProtocolAlpha.
adjust_protocol_liquidity then calls update_weights_for_added_liquidity: new w_quote = q2/(q1+q2), with q1 = w_base*y*(x+dx) and q2 = w_quote*x*(y+dy). Any amount that would push a weight outside [0.01, 0.99] is parked in BalancerTaoReservoir / BalancerAlphaReservoir.
Live check on SN51: issuance 6.086M and rp = 0.9818M/(0.9818M+6.086M) = 0.139, so alpha_in = 0.139/block, tao_in = 0.01397 and chain buy = 0.05148 TAO/block. These match SubnetTaoInEmission and SubnetExcessTao.
Live inputs: SubnetTAO[0] = 5,454,346 TAO; TaoWeight = 3,320,413,933,267,719,290/u64::MAX = 0.18 (code default about 5.27%).
sources: mainnet storage TaoWeight, SubnetTAO[0], SubnetTaoInEmission, SubnetExcessTao

verification.evidence: In run_coinbase.rs get_subnet_terms, alpha_in = E/price, capped at root_proportion*alpha_emission, and excess = E − tao_in. inject_and_maybe_swap calls swap_tao_for_alpha(max_price, drop_fees=true) and the bought alpha goes to SubnetProtocolAlpha. block_step.rs root_proportion = (SubnetTAO[0]*TaoWeight)/(that + get_alpha_issuance), where issuance includes the alpha reservoir. impls.rs adjust_protocol_liquidity and balancer.rs update_weights_for_added_liquidity give q1 = w_base*y*(x+dx), q2 = w_quote*x*(y+dy), new w_quote = q2/(q1+q2); out-of-range amounts go to the reservoirs. Live at block 9,240,382: SN51 rp 0.1389, taoin 0.013973, excess 0.051494, alpha_in 0.1389. SubnetTAO[0] = 5,454,229. TaoWeight raw 3320413933267719290 = 0.18; the runtime default is 971718665099567868 (~5.27%).

findings.claim: alpha_out is 1 alpha per block per emitting subnet at the current (pre-alpha-halving) rate, whatever the subnet's TAO share. Tail subnets below the gate therefore get dilution with almost no TAO injection or protocol buybacks.
findings.detail:
alpha_out_i = get_block_emission_for_issuance(alpha_issuance_i), where alpha_issuance = SubnetAlphaIn + SubnetAlphaOut + alpha reservoir. It is minted every block for every subnet in subnets_to_emit_to, including subnets whose TAO emission is disabled or gated to about 0.
Live: SubnetAlphaOutEmission = 1.0 for every subnet, so 7,200 alpha/day each. The largest alpha issuance is about 6.27M (SN28), below the 10.5M halving threshold.
Example (derived): SN92 has TAO reserve 587 and price 0.00135. Its 7,200 alpha/day is worth about 9.7 TAO/day of potential sell flow, about 1.65% of its TAO reserve per day, while its TAO emission is about 0.
The docs state a young subnet mints up to 2 alpha/block in total: alpha_out (1) plus alpha_in (at most root_prop × 1).

verification.correction: The mechanism and the SN92 dilution numbers are right. The largest alpha issuance is SN4 at about 6.41M (AlphaIn+AlphaOut), followed by SN64 at 6.39M, SN12 at 6.38M and SN28 at 6.27M. SN28 has the largest AlphaOut (5.25M). All are still below the 10.5M alpha halving threshold. SubnetAlphaOutEmission is 1.0 for every emitting subnet and 0 for the three subnets without start_call (59, 82, 86). 18% of alpha_out is the owner cut, which is auto-locked to conviction, so not all 7,200 alpha/day is immediately sellable.
verification.evidence: run_coinbase.rs emit_to_subnets mints alpha_out = get_block_emission_for_issuance(get_alpha_issuance) for every subnet in subnets_to_emit_to, regardless of SubnetEmissionEnabled. The live snapshot (block 9,240,380) has issuance maxima of SN4 6,405,573, SN64 6,389,047, SN12 6,378,027 and SN28 6,274,618. SN92: 7,200 × 0.0013482 = 9.71 TAO/day, which is 1.65% of the 587.2 TAO reserve. emissions.mdx says 'a young subnet mints up to 2 alpha per block'.

findings.claim: How alpha_out is split: 18% owner cut, then 50/50 between miners and validators. A root_proportion share of the validator half goes to root stakers, and only while Σ EMA prices > 1. The split is paid out at each tempo boundary (default 360 blocks).
findings.detail:
Owner cut = SubnetOwnerCut/65535, default 11,796 (18%); unset on-chain, so the default applies. It is applied only if the subnet has owner cut enabled, can be auto-locked into conviction, and is paid to the owner hotkey.
From the remaining a' = 0.82*alpha_out:
- miners: 0.5*a'
- root_alpha = root_proportion*0.5*a'
- alpha-staker validators: 0.5*a' - root_alpha
The root alpha accrues only if get_network_root_sell_flag is true, meaning Σ SubnetMovingPrice over eligible subnets > 1.0 (live: 1.1854). Otherwise it is recycled.
Pending amounts accumulate (PendingServerEmission, PendingValidatorEmission, PendingRootAlphaDivs, PendingOwnerCut) and drain at the epoch, which fires when Tempo blocks have passed since the last epoch.
Tempo defaults to 360 and owners can set 360–50,400. Live: 124 subnets at 360; legacy subnets at 99, 100, 1440, 1800 and 7200.
At most MaxEpochsPerBlock = 2 epochs run per block; extra epochs are deferred one block.
If total miner incentive in an epoch is 0, validators also receive the miner half.
Miner incentive sent to owner hotkeys is burned or recycled, and that fraction becomes MinerBurned for the A4 emission scaling.
sources: mainnet storage SubnetOwnerCut (unset), Tempo, MaxEpochsPerBlock (unset → prod default 2)

verification.correction:
The split logic is correct. Two details are off.
(1) Live tempos on the 128 non-root subnets: 124 at 360, plus one each at 99, 1440, 1800 and 7200. There is no non-root subnet at 100.
(2) The per-block epoch cap is MaxEpochsPerBlock = 2 (unset, prod default). It drops to 1 in any block where a Null-consensus epoch is due. Owners can also trigger early epochs (PendingEpochAt).
verification.evidence: emit_to_subnets: owner_cut = alpha_out*cut only if OwnerCutEnabled; root_alpha = rp*0.5*(alpha_out − cut); server = 0.5*rest; validator = rest − server − root_alpha. Root alpha goes to PendingRootAlphaDivs only when root_sell_flag is set (Σ EMA > 1; live 1.18537); otherwise it is recycled. distribute_emission gives validators the server alpha too when incentive_sum == 0. findings.claim: Alpha staking yield: each validator hotkey's dividend is split between an alpha share and a root share by stake mix. Nominators receive the alpha share minus the validator take, auto-compounded as alpha.
findings.detail:
calculate_dividend_distribution, for each hotkey dividend d:
- alpha_divs = d * alpha_stake/(alpha_stake + root_stake*TaoWeight).
- root_divs = d - alpha_divs, but only if the hotkey has a root UID; otherwise that slice is unassigned.
- The pool sizes are then fixed: Σ alpha_divs maps pro-rata onto pending_validator_alpha, and Σ root_divs onto pending_root_alpha.
For each hotkey, take = Delegates[hotkey] (default and maximum 18% = 11,796/65535, minimum 0; MaxDelegateTake and MinDelegateTake unset on-chain). Nominator alpha = alpha_divs*(1 - take), credited to the hotkey's share pool through increase_stake_for_hotkey_on_subnet, so it compounds pro-rata by shares.
Stake weight for consensus = alpha_stake + root_stake*0.18. Validator permits go to the top-K by stake weight (K = 128 by default, 64 on new subnets). The StakeThreshold on-chain is 1e12 rao (1,000).
Rough yield (derived): alpha APR ≈ 0.41*(1 - rp)*7,200*365/total_alpha_staked*(1 - take). For SN92: rp ≈ 0.48, giving about 89% per year in alpha terms before take. Alpha supply grows by 7,200/day at the same time, so TAO-denominated yield depends entirely on price.

verification.evidence: calculate_dividend_distribution: alpha_divs = d*alpha/(alpha + root*tao_weight); root_divs only if Uids(ROOT, hotkey) exists, otherwise unassigned. Pools are pro-rata to pending_alpha and pending_root_alpha. distribute_dividends_and_incentives: nominator_divs = alpha_divs*(1 − take), credited through increase_stake_for_hotkey_on_subnet (share pool). Stake weight = alpha + tao*tao_weight, using inherited stakes. Runtime SubtensorInitialDefaultTake = 11,796 and MinDelegateTake = 0; both are unset on chain. MaxAllowedValidators initial is 128, and init_new_network sets 64. StakeThreshold on chain = 1e12. The APR figure is a rough derived estimate: it uses AlphaOut as the staked base, but AlphaOut also contains protocol-owned alpha.

findings.claim: Root (netuid 0) yield under Root Reborn (v441, July 2026): root dividends are paid in alpha into a per-validator basket ('beta' shares). They are no longer force-sold every block. Stakers realize TAO only when they claim.
findings.detail:
Each epoch, a validator's root alpha dividend minus its take is enqueued (enqueue_basket_deposit) and credited into that validator's fund. The fund's holdings are ordinary alpha stake held by a keyless escrow account. Stakers own β shares, valued at realizable net asset value (NAV).
claim_root_with_hotkey sells the claimant's pro-rata slice of every holding to TAO at pool price and restakes it on root. The claim threshold defaults to 500,000 rao.
Validators may trade holdings with swap_basket. BasketTradingEnabled is true on-chain. Guardrails: 2% per-leg price band against the moving and fast-moving prices, turnover limit of 10% of NAV per day, 10% per-pool liquidity cap, and a concentration cap (on-chain BasketConcentrationCap raw value 7,865, which I did not decode).
Root staking itself is 1:1, no fee, no slippage. RootStakeUnlockInterval is unset (0), so there is no hold window.
Market effect: mechanical sell pressure from root dividends has been replaced by intermittent sells at claim and trade time.

verification.correction:
The mechanism is right, with these fixes.
(1) v441 is labelled 'July 2026' but went live at block 8,765,683 on 2026-08-03 19:18Z.
(2) The swap_basket 2% band (BASKET_TRADE_MAX_SLIPPAGE_BPS = 200) uses the strictest of three references: slow EMA, fast EMA and spot.
(3) BasketConcentrationCap raw 7,865 is u16-normalized: 7865/65535 ≈ 12.0% of fund NAV. The code default is 4096 (1/16), the value the docs give for launch.
(4) The claim threshold is RootClaimableThreshold[ROOT] (default 500,000 rao), and auto-claim is off.
(5) BasketMinTradeTao on chain is 5,000,000 rao (0.005 TAO); the code default is 0.5 TAO.
(6) Trading via swap_basket arrived in spec 461 (September 2026).
verification.evidence: root-reborn.mdx: dividends are credited into per-validator escrowed funds with no sell; NAV is realizable; a claim pays 'TAO staked back to root'; root staking has no fee and no slippage. run_coinbase.rs: the root take goes to the validator, and the remainder goes through enqueue_basket_deposit. lib.rs: DEFAULT_BASKET_DAILY_TURNOVER_CAP = u16::MAX/10 and DEFAULT_BASKET_LIQUIDITY_CAP = u16::MAX/10 (both unset on chain); RootStakeUnlockInterval is a ValueQuery with no default (0), unset on chain; BasketTradingEnabled = 0x01. The archive node gives the spec 441 deploy block.

findings.claim: TAO supply schedule: 21M cap. Halvings are triggered by total issuance crossing thresholds, not by block counts. The first halving happened at block 7,103,975 (2025-12-15 13:31 UTC). Block emission is now 0.5 TAO; the next halving is at 15.75M issuance.
findings.detail:
get_block_emission_for_issuance(I) = floor(1e9 rao * 2^-floor(log2(1/(1 - I/21e15)))), returning 0 at or above TotalSupply. The halving thresholds are 10.5M, 15.75M, 18.375M, and so on.
Recycled TAO (registration burns and fees since v445) reduces issuance and pushes halvings later. Burned TAO does not.
Live values: TotalIssuance = 11,597,577.84 TAO (Balances and Subtensor agree). Total subnet emission summed to 0.50000 TAO/block.
I found the halving block by binary-searching TotalIssuance on the archive node. Secondary news sources (COINOTAG) agree on a Dec 15, 2025 completion.
Estimate (derived): the next halving is about 4.15M TAO away, about 1,150+ days at 3,600/day, so roughly 2029 or later.

verification.evidence: In block_emission.rs, emission = DefaultBlockEmission/2^floor(log2(1/(1 − I/21e15))), and 0 at or above TotalSupply. Archive data: TotalIssuance after block 7,103,974 was 10,499,999.689; after block 7,103,975 it was 10,500,000.688 (Timestamp 2025-12-15T13:31:24Z); block 7,103,976 added about 0.4986. So the crossing happened in block 7,103,975, and 7,103,976 was the first 0.5-TAO block. Live at block ~9,240,363: SubtensorModule.TotalIssuance = 11,597,611.13 and Balances = 11,597,611.63, about 0.5 TAO apart. emissions.mdx: recycling pushes halvings out and burned TAO stays in issuance. 15.75M − 11.598M = 4.15M TAO, about 1,153 days at 3,600/day.

findings.claim: Each subnet's alpha follows the same 21M-cap, issuance-triggered halving curve. A TAO halving also halves every pool's injection.
findings.detail:
The same function is applied to alpha_issuance = SubnetAlphaIn + SubnetAlphaOut + reservoir (A8). The first alpha halving comes at 10.5M issuance for that subnet; no subnet has reached it (maximum about 6.3M).
Because tao_in follows the halved TAO emission and alpha_in = tao_in/price, the Dec-2025 TAO halving also halved alpha_in.
Recycled alpha reduces issuance. Burned alpha (for example owner-hotkey miner emission under RecycleOrBurn = Burn, or the stake_burn buyback) stays counted.
'Moving price' means SubnetMovingPrice, the slow EMA in A6. The SDK reads stake value at spot (alpha × price).

findings.claim: Subnet registration cost doubles on each registration and decays linearly. The pool is seeded with the full lock at the median alpha price. Live: about 969 TAO. On-chain parameters differ from the docs: the floor is 1 TAO, not 1,000 TAO.
findings.detail:
lock_cost = max(min_lock, 2*last_lock - (last_lock/interval_eff)*(now - last_lock_block)), where interval_eff = NetworkLockReductionInterval * (block_emission/1e9).
On-chain values: NetworkMinLockCost = 1,000,000,000 rao (1 TAO); NetworkLastLockCost = 653.02 TAO; NetworkLockReductionInterval = 115,200, which becomes an effective 57,600 blocks after the halving. So the cost returns to last_lock after 8 days and to the floor after 16 days.
The runtime API SubnetRegistrationRuntimeApi_get_network_registration_cost returned 969.383 TAO at block about 9,240,300.
NetworkRateLimit = 14,400 blocks (about 2 days), applied network-wide through the last-lock block. The docs say 7,200.
At registration the entire lock becomes SubnetTAO, and SubnetAlphaIn = lock/median_subnet_alpha_price, so a new subnet starts at the median spot price but with EMA = 0.
SubnetEmissionEnabled is set to false at registration, and only root/governance can enable it. Live: SN35, 36, 82, 108 and 116 (recent) and SN29 are disabled. SN36 has been disabled for about 49 days.
StartCallDelay is unset, so 0: the owner can call start_call immediately. start_call sets FirstEmissionBlockNumber = now + 1 and SubtokenEnabled = true. Until then the subnet has no trading, no emission and no EMA updates.

verification.evidence: root.rs get_network_lock_cost = max(min_lock, last*mult − (last/interval_eff)*(now − last_block)), with mult = 2 (or 1 if last_block == 0). get_lock_reduction_interval scales by block_emission/1e9. On chain: NetworkMinLockCost 1e9, NetworkLastLockCost 653,019,966,758, NetworkLockReductionInterval 115,200, NetworkRateLimit 14,400. Runtime defaults: 1000 TAO min lock, 7200 rate limit, 14*7200 reduction interval. rate_limiting.rs keys RegisterNetwork on get_network_last_lock_block (network-wide). The runtime API returned 968.442 TAO at block 9,240,388, consistent with linear decay from 969.383. set_new_network_state: SubnetTAO = lock, SubnetAlphaIn = lock/median price, SubnetEmissionEnabled = false. sudo_set_subnet_emission_enabled requires ensure_root. StartCallDelay is unset, so the runtime default 0 applies. do_start_call sets FirstEmissionBlockNumber = now+1 and SubtokenEnabled = true. Live disabled set: 29, 35, 36, 82, 108, 116; SN36 registered 356k blocks (~49 days) ago. Nuance: validate_remove_stake has its subtoken check commented out; validate_add_stake enforces it.

findings.claim: Subnet cap and pruning: SubnetLimit is 128 on-chain and full. Each new registration dissolves the non-immune subnet with the lowest SubnetMovingPrice, with ties going to the earliest registered. Immunity is 864,000 blocks (about 120 days).
findings.detail:
do_register_network: if the count of non-root subnets plus the cleanup queue is at least SubnetLimit, it picks get_network_to_prune(). That function skips subnets where now < NetworkRegisteredAt + NetworkImmunityPeriod and picks the minimum get_moving_alpha_price. If every subnet is immune, it fails with SubnetLimitReached.
On-chain: SubnetLimit = 128 (code default 128). TotalNetworks = 129 including root. NetworkImmunityPeriod = 864,000; the code default and docs say 1,296,000. There is no inactivity-based deregistration.
Conflict: the commit for 'release v440' says 'subnet limit 256', but the chain shows 128 and the v440 release page says raising the cap is deferred.
Combined with the 14,400-block rate limit, at most one prune happens about every 2 days.
Derived from the snapshot at block 9,240,299: the current prune candidate is SN92, with EMA 0.001359, registered at 8,352,006 and non-immune since about 9,216,006.
Subnets with no start_call (SN59, 82, 86) have EMA 0 and are pruned first once their immunity ends.

verification.evidence: do_register_network: if count + cleanup_queue ≥ SubnetLimit, it either waits for cleanup or calls get_network_to_prune, failing with SubnetLimitReached if none is found. get_network_to_prune skips subnets inside the immunity window, picks the minimum moving price, and breaks ties by earliest registered_at. On chain: SubnetLimit 128, TotalNetworks 129, NetworkImmunityPeriod 864,000; the runtime default is 1,296,000. Commit 791e9999 is titled 'release v440: emission gate, subnet limit 256', but the v440 page says raising the cap is deferred. SubnetInfoRuntimeApi_get_subnet_to_prune returned Some(92). SN92 registered at 8,352,006 and has been non-immune since 9,216,006, with EMA 0.0013584. SN59, 82 and 86 have no start_call and are still immune.

findings.claim: What alpha holders get on deregistration: TAO credited straight to each coldkey from the pool's TAO reserve, pro-rata by alpha value. The denominator also includes pool and protocol alpha, and validator baskets are sold through the pool first. Holders typically receive far less than spot.
findings.detail:
Dissolve phases, in order:
0. do_dissolve_network moves the reservoirs into the reserves.
1. Phase SubnetBasketHoldingsToRoot sells every validator's basket alpha on this subnet through the AMM (sell_basket_alpha_for_root_tao), which drains SubnetTAO first.
2. The pot is the remaining SubnetTAO. Each staker (hotkey, coldkey) receives pot * alpha_val / total_alpha_value (largest-remainder rounding), credited as free TAO, not restaked. Conviction locks are deleted and accumulated conviction is lost.
3. total_alpha_value = Σ staker alpha value + protocol term. For subnets registered after TaoInRefundDeploymentBlock (8,334,450, 2026-06-04) the protocol term is SubnetAlphaIn + SubnetProtocolAlpha; for legacy subnets it is SubnetProtocolAlpha only.
4. The protocol's share, plus any leftover, is recycled. Owners of subnets registered before NetworkRegistrationStartBlock (6,573,966) get a lock refund of lock - owner_emission_value.
Implied value per alpha ≈ SubnetTAO/(AlphaOut + AlphaIn + ProtocolAlpha), compared with spot ≈ SubnetTAO/AlphaIn. For SN92 (derived): 587.2/1,108,690 ≈ 0.00053 against spot 0.00135, a haircut of about 61%. For SN47 (legacy): about 0.00062 against 0.0017, about 64%.
Real example: SN108 was dissolved at block 9,111,229 (2026-09-20).

verification.correction:
The payout mechanics are right, but the implied-value formula double-counts protocol alpha. Chain buys add the bought alpha to both SubnetAlphaOut and SubnetProtocolAlpha, and that alpha is not staked to any hotkey. So Σ staker alpha ≈ AlphaOut − ProtocolAlpha (minus pending emission).
- New subnets: value per alpha ≈ SubnetTAO/(AlphaOut + AlphaIn). For SN92 that is 587.2/1,067,584 ≈ 0.00055, a haircut of about 59% (not 0.00053 and 61%).
- Legacy subnets: ≈ SubnetTAO/AlphaOut. For SN47: 983.9/1,576,160 ≈ 0.00062, a haircut of about 64% (as stated).
Basket sales happen first and further reduce the pot.
verification.evidence: dissolution.rs: do_dissolve_network folds the reservoirs into reserves; the default phase is SubnetBasketHoldingsToRoot (claim_root.rs convert_subnet_basket_holdings_to_root, then sell_basket_alpha_for_root_tao). remove_stake.rs get_total_alpha_value: the protocol term is AlphaIn + ProtocolAlpha if reg_at > TaoInRefundDeploymentBlock, otherwise ProtocolAlpha. settle_stakes uses pot = SubnetTAO with largest-remainder rounding, credited to coldkey free balance. destroy_alpha_in_out_stakes: legacy refund = lock − owner_emission_tao if reg_at < NetworkRegistrationStartBlock; the remainder is recycled; lock phases are cleared. On chain: TaoInRefundDeploymentBlock = 8,334,450 and NetworkRegistrationStartBlock = 6,573,966. Archive: NetworksAdded[108] was true at 9,111,228 and absent at 9,111,229 (2026-09-20T20:46:48Z); SN108 was re-registered at 9,111,253.

findings.claim: Subnets that burn all miner incentive, have TAO emission disabled, or have registration disabled get no TAO emission. Under the gate, only about the top 35–40 subnets by price EMA receive meaningful TAO.
findings.detail:
Live snapshot: 125 eligible subnets, 99 with a positive burn-adjusted share, theta = 0.00826.
- Top 8 subnets: about 52% of emission.
- Subnets ranked about 40 and below: under 0.1% each.
- About 26 subnets have MinerBurned = 1, so 0 TAO.
- 6 subnets have SubnetEmissionEnabled = false.
- Subnets with NetworkRegistrationAllowed = false are dropped from subnets_to_emit_to entirely, so they get no alpha_out either.
The v440 notes cite these effects: the share of emission going to subnets below the bar fell from 38.4% to 12.5%, and the effective subnet count from about 50 to about 22. Near the bar the response is strong: a subnet at rank 36 that raises demand 10% gains about 26% more emission (secondary, from the release notes).
Because the price EMA has an 8-hour half-life (A6), there is a reflexive loop: buying raises the EMA, which raises emission and chain buys, which raise price.

verification.evidence: Live (block 9,240,382): 125 eligible subnets, 99 positive burn-adjusted shares, theta 0.0082624. 26 subnets have MinerBurned ≥ 1. 6 have emission disabled. None currently have NetworkRegistrationAllowed = false (the filter exists in get_subnets_to_emit_to). Top 8 by emission: 53.1%. Rank 40 by emission: 0.0987%. 39 subnets are at or above 0.1%. The top 40 receive 99.2%. The v440 page shows 38.4% to 12.5%, effective count ~50 to ~22, and 'a subnet at rank 36 that grows its demand 10% gains roughly 26% more emission'.

findings.claim: Execution features you can use: add_stake_limit / remove_stake_limit with allow_partial; an on-chain LimitOrders pallet (enabled) with relayer-executed LimitBuy, TakeProfit and StopLoss orders; and MEV-shielded submission (ML-KEM-768). There is no per-block staking rate limit in validate_add_stake / validate_remove_stake.
findings.detail:
add_stake_limit (call_index 88) takes (hotkey, netuid, amount_staked, limit_price in rao per alpha, allow_partial). The chain fills up to the limit using the delta_in formulas in A2.
LimitOrders (pallet index 32): LimitOrdersEnabled = true on-chain. Users sign VersionedOrder V1 or V2 off-chain with fields signer, hotkey, netuid, order_type, amount, limit_price, expiry (ms), fee_rate (Perbill), fee_recipient, relayer and max_slippage. A relayer submits execute_orders, or execute_batched_orders, which nets buys against sells and swaps only the residual against the pool.
MEV shield: pallet MevShield (index 30); the SDK call is client.submit_shielded(intent, wallet). The block author decrypts and includes the transaction.
Locked conviction alpha or collateral-bonded alpha cannot be unstaked (ensure_available_to_unstake).

verification.evidence: dispatches.rs: call_index 88 add_stake_limit(hotkey, netuid, amount_staked: TaoBalance, limit_price: TaoBalance, allow_partial: bool); remove_stake_limit has the same shape with AlphaBalance. validate_add_stake and validate_remove_stake contain no rate limit, and the CheckRateLimits guard covers only weights and register_network. The limit-orders README covers VersionedOrder V1/V2, the order fields, LimitBuy/TakeProfit/StopLoss, and execute_batched_orders netting. construct_runtime: MevShield = 30, LimitOrders = 32, Swap = 28, SubtensorModule = 7. The shield pallet uses MlKem768 + XChaCha20-Poly1305. advanced.mdx: `await client.submit_shielded(intent, wallet)`. unstake paths call ensure_available_to_unstake and ensure_hotkey_covers_collateral. LimitOrders.LimitOrdersEnabled = 0x01.

findings.claim: Subnet ownership can be taken over by 'conviction' (time-weighted alpha locks): v431, revised in v447. The owner cut can also be auto-locked.
findings.detail:
change_subnet_owner_if_needed runs at each epoch. In v431: if the subnet is more than 1 year old and total conviction exceeds 10% of outstanding alpha, ownership (including the 18% cut) passes to the hotkey with the most conviction. v447 changed the gate to a single hotkey measured against an 18% threshold.
Lock types: perpetual locks have a maturity time constant of about 43 days; decaying locks unlock with a time constant of about 130 days. Both are governance-set.
This matters for valuing older micro-caps: an ownership change can redirect the owner's emission and miner-burn behavior. MinerBurned also changes emission (A4).

api_details:
=== LIVE PARAMETERS (finney, block ~9,240,300, 2026-10-08) ===
Chain and supply:
- specVersion 475
- TotalIssuance 11,597,577.84 TAO
- block emission 0.5 TAO
- TotalStake 7,437,105 TAO
- SubnetTAO[0] (root) 5,454,346 TAO

Emission and pricing:
- TaoWeight 0.18 (raw 3320413933267719290 / u64::MAX)
- SubnetMovingAlpha 0.0003 (I96F32 raw 1288490)
- EMAPriceHalvingBlocks 201,600 (default for every subnet)
- EmissionGateExponent h = 3 (default)
- EmissionBarRank N = 32 (default; rank mode)
- EmissionBarQuantile 0.75 (ignored in rank mode)
- EmissionGateBar theta = 0.0082624 (U64F64)
- SubnetOwnerCut 11796/65535
- FeeRate 33/65535 on every subnet

Lifecycle:
- SubnetLimit 128; TotalNetworks 129 (including root)
- NetworkImmunityPeriod 864,000 blocks
- NetworkMinLockCost 1 TAO; NetworkLastLockCost 653.02 TAO
- NetworkLockReductionInterval 115,200 (effective 57,600 after the halving)
- NetworkRateLimit 14,400 blocks
- StartCallDelay 0
- MaxEpochsPerBlock 2
- TaoInRefundDeploymentBlock 8,334,450; NetworkRegistrationStartBlock 6,573,966

Root and execution:
- BasketTradingEnabled true
- LimitOrders.LimitOrdersEnabled true
- RootStakeUnlockInterval 0
- live registration cost 969.383 TAO

Event blocks:
- first halving: block 7,103,975 (2025-12-15T13:31Z)
- Taoflow EMA frozen at block 8,466,530 (2026-06-23T01:25Z)

=== PYTHON SIMULATION FORMULAS (rao integers; 1 TAO = 1e9 rao) ===
x = SubnetAlphaIn[n]; y = SubnetTAO[n]; wq = SwapBalancer[n].quote / 1e18 (0.5 by default); wb = 1 - wq; f = FeeRate[n] (33)
spot = (wb/wq) * y / x   # the runtime API returns this x1e9 as u64

def buy(tao_in):  # stake
    fee = tao_in * f // 65535; dy = tao_in - fee
    assert dy <= 1000*y and x >= 1_000_000
    a_out = x * (1 - (y/(y+dy))**(wq/wb))   # wq = 0.5 gives x*dy/(y+dy)
    # new reserves: y += dy ; x -= a_out ; the fee goes to the block author

def sell(a_in):  # unstake
    fee = a_in * f // 65535; dx = a_in - fee
    t_out = y * (1 - (x/(x+dx))**(wb/wq))
    x1, y1 = x+dx, y-t_out
    t_fee = y1 * (1 - (x1/(x1+fee))**(wb/wq))   # fee alpha sold fee-free; TAO paid to the author
    # final reserves: x = x1 + fee ; y = y1 - t_fee ; the user receives t_out

Fill size before hitting a limit price:
- buy up to p': dy = y * ((p'/p)**wb - 1)
- sell down to p': dx = x * ((p/p')**wq - 1)
- when the limit binds, fee = delta * f/(65535 - f)

Injection (per block, per enabled subnet i):
- E_i = 0.5 TAO * final_share_i
- rp_i = (SubnetTAO[0]*TaoWeight) / (SubnetTAO[0]*TaoWeight + AlphaIn_i + AlphaOut_i + alpha_reservoir_i)
- a_in = min(E_i/spot_i, rp_i * alpha_emission_i); tao_in = a_in*spot_i if capped, else E_i
- excess = E_i - tao_in, swapped TAO→alpha with no fee (chain buy)
- injection re-solves the weights: new wq = q2/(q1+q2), with q1 = wb*y*(x+da) and q2 = wq*x*(y+dt); spot price is unchanged

Emission share:
- s_i = ema_i/Σema
- b_i = s_i*(1 - min(MinerBurned_i, 1)), renormalized
- g_i = b_i/(1 + (theta/b_i)**3)
- final_i = g_i / Σ_enabled g
- theta = Nth-largest positive b (N = 32), recomputed when block % 360 == 0

EMA (per block):
- a = 0.0003 * B/(B + 201600), with B = block - (FirstEmissionBlockNumber - 1)
- ema = a*min(spot, 1.0) + (1 - a)*ema

Alpha and TAO emission for issuance I:
- 1e9 * 2**(-floor(log2(1/(1 - I/21e15))))

alpha_out split per block:
- owner 0.18
- remainder r = 0.82: miners 0.5r; root rp*0.5r (only if Σema > 1, else recycled); alpha validators 0.5r*(1 - rp)
- paid out each Tempo (360 blocks)

Hotkey dividend split:
- alpha part = d*α/(α + τ*0.18); root part = rest (only if the hotkey holds a root UID)
- nominator alpha share = alpha part * (1 - take); take ≤ 18%

Lock cost:
- max(min_lock, 2*last - last/(115200*E/1e9)*(now - last_block))

Prune:
- argmin SubnetMovingPrice among subnets where now ≥ NetworkRegisteredAt + 864000

Deregistration payout per staker:
- SubnetTAO_after_basket_sales * alpha_i / (Σ staker alpha + [AlphaIn if registered > 8,334,450] + ProtocolAlpha)

=== RUNTIME APIs (state_call; SCALE-encoded params) ===
- SwapRuntimeApi_current_alpha_price(netuid: u16) -> u64 (rao per alpha, i.e. price x1e9)

api_corrections:
1. SubnetFastMovingPrice has a different type from SubnetMovingPrice. It is U64F64 stored as a u128: divide by 2^64. It is an OptionQuery and is absent until the first update. Do not decode it as I96F32/2^32.

2. NominatorMinRequiredStake is a per-million factor of DefaultMinStake. The on-chain raw value 10,000,000 means 0.02 TAO, not 0.01 TAO.

3. `btcli subnets bar` does not exist in the current monorepo CLI. The subnets commands are list, show, hyperparameters, burn-cost, create-cost, price, conviction, register, create and metagraph. There is also no emission-bar query doc. Read SubtensorModule.EmissionGateBar (U64F64/2^64) from storage instead.

4. `sub.subnets.subnet_tao_flows()` / SubnetEmaTaoFlow has been frozen since spec 421 at block 8,466,530 (2026-06-23), not since v431. Subnets registered after that date have no entry.

5. Emission-share history for backtests, by spec:
   - spec ≤ 419: flow-based.
   - spec 421 (block 8,466,530): price_EMA × root_proportion × (1 − MinerBurned), no gate.
   - spec 432, the 'v431' release (block 8,636,190, 2026-07-16): price_EMA × (1 − MinerBurned).
   - spec 440 (block 8,713,793): adds the Hill gate.
   - spec 444 was never deployed. Spec 443 ran from 8,772,666 to 8,831,002, then spec 445.

6. First halving: issuance crossed 10.5M inside block 7,103,975 (10,500,000.69 after it). The first 0.5 TAO block is 7,103,976.

7. Deregistration value per alpha: SubnetAlphaOut already includes SubnetProtocolAlpha, so the staker alpha base is about AlphaOut − ProtocolAlpha. The new-subnet denominator is therefore about AlphaOut + AlphaIn. Do not add ProtocolAlpha again.

8. Tempo values on non-root subnets are 360 (124 subnets), 99, 1440, 1800 and 7200. There is none at 100.

9. Largest alpha issuance is SN4 at about 6.41M, not SN28 at 6.27M.

10. Missing runtime APIs:
   - SubnetInfoRuntimeApi_get_subnet_to_prune() -> Option<NetUid> (returned 92 live)
   - SubnetInfoRuntimeApi_get_next_epoch_start_block(netuid)
   - SubnetInfoRuntimeApi_get_block_emission()
   - StakeInfoRuntimeApi_get_stake_fee(...)

11. SimSwapResult field semantics: for a buy, tao_amount = net TAO in after the fee and alpha_amount = alpha out. For a sell, alpha_amount = net alpha in and tao_amount = TAO out. alpha_fee/tao_fee hold the fee on the input side, and *_slippage is price impact on the output side.

12. Missing SDK read: sub.subnets.subnet_registration_cost(). The epoch-related reads epochs.next_epoch_start_block / blocks_until_next_epoch also exist.

13. add_stake_burn is call_index 132: (hotkey, netuid, amount: TaoBalance, limit: Option<TaoBalance>). start_call is call_index 92.

14. SDK v11 stake intents apply a default 5% price bound unless you opt out, so expect SlippageTooHigh.

15. Basket parameters: BasketConcentrationCap 7865/65535 ≈ 12.0%. BasketMinTradeTao on chain is 0.005 TAO (code default 0.5 TAO). The swap_basket band is 2% from the strictest of slow EMA, fast EMA and spot.

16. Endpoints:
   - entrypoint-finney keeps at least 300 blocks of state; 1,000 blocks back is already discarded.
   - archive.chain.opentensor.ai accepts HTTP JSON-RPC but enforces HTTP 429 plus a 'Historical work rate limit exceeded' (code -32004) budget, so throttle backtest pulls.
   - https://lite.chain.opentensor.ai answers HTTP JSON-RPC.
missed_critical_facts: For any backtest of TAO emission, the regime from 2026-06-23 to 2026-07-16 (spec 421, blocks 8,466,530 to 8,636,189) used shares ∝ price_EMA × root_proportion × (1 − MinerBurned). I reproduced this exactly at block 8,550,000. In that window, 64 of 128 subnets had SubnetEmissionEnabled = false. Root-proportion weighting strongly favored young subnets with low alpha issuance. Source: https://archive.chain.opentensor.ai (state at block 8,550,000) and commit eaadb745a0 at https://api.github.com/repos/RaoFoundation/subtensor/commits?path=pallets/subtensor/src/coinbase/subnet_emissions.rs

Mainnet runtime upgrade blocks, needed to align regimes in backtests:
- spec 421: block 8,466,530 (2026-06-23 01:25Z)
- spec 432 ('v431' release): 8,636,190 (2026-07-16 19:30Z)
- spec 440: 8,713,793 (2026-07-27 14:16Z)
- spec 441: 8,765,683 (2026-08-03 19:18Z)
- spec 443: 8,772,666 (2026-08-04)
- spec 445: 8,831,003 (2026-08-12 21:06Z)
- spec 446: 8,843,319 (2026-08-14)
Spec 444 never ran on mainnet. Source: archive.chain.opentensor.ai, state_getRuntimeVersion and Timestamp.Now

The SDK v11 stake intents apply a default 5% price bound unless you opt out, so expect SlippageTooHigh. Limit stakes refund unswapped TAO to the coldkey, so read post-state balances rather than StakeAdded. When fees are paid in alpha, do not submit the full alpha balance. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RaoFoundation/subtensor/main/website/apps/bittensor-website/src/app/(pages-without-footer)/releases/v431-upgrade/page.tsx

Pruning and registration are asynchronous. register_network on a full network dissolves the prune target immediately, but it queues the new subnet (NetworkRegistrationQueued, via NetworkRegistrationQueue and DissolveCleanupQueue). Dissolution payouts run over multiple blocks in metered on_idle cleanup phases, with basket sales first. Monitor NetworkRemoved and NetworkAdded events. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RaoFoundation/subtensor/main/pallets/subtensor/src/subnets/subnet.rs and dissolution.rs

A runtime API returns the current prune candidate directly: SubnetInfoRuntimeApi_get_subnet_to_prune() returned Some(92) live. With the network-wide registration cost decaying to as low as 1 TAO after 16 idle days, prune risk for the lowest-EMA non-immune subnet can materialize cheaply. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RaoFoundation/subtensor/main/pallets/subtensor/runtime-api/src/lib.rs

SubnetAlphaOut includes protocol-owned alpha. Chain buys increment both SubnetAlphaOut and SubnetProtocolAlpha, and that alpha is not staked to any hotkey. Float, yield and deregistration calculations should use AlphaOut − ProtocolAlpha as the staker base. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RaoFoundation/subtensor/main/pallets/subtensor/src/staking/stake_utils.rs and coinbase/run_coinbase.rs

The owner cut (18% of alpha_out) is auto-locked to conviction (auto_lock_owner_cut), so it is not immediately sell pressure. Subnet ownership is now conviction-based, and subnets older than one year are contestable. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RaoFoundation/subtensor/main/pallets/subtensor/src/coinbase/run_coinbase.rs and v431 release page

Owners can switch subnets to EpochConsensus::Null, where a single top-stake validator sets weights and Yuma and bonds are skipped. When a Null epoch is due, the per-block epoch cap drops to 1. Owners can also trigger early epochs (PendingEpochAt), so tempo-boundary timing is not strictly every Tempo blocks. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RaoFoundation/subtensor/main/docs/guides/null-consensus.mdx and run_coinbase.rs

Data infrastructure limits for backtesting. The public entrypoint discards state older than a few hundred blocks: it worked at 300 blocks back and failed at 1,000. The public archive node rate-limits with HTTP 429 and a JSON-RPC -32004 'Historical work rate limit exceeded' budget. Plan on an indexer (Taostats or tao.app) or your own archive node for history. Source: live RPC tests against https://entrypoint-finney.opentensor.ai and https://archive.chain.opentensor.ai

Staking requires SubtokenEnabled. validate_remove_stake has the subtoken check commented out, so unstaking is not blocked by it. Neither path has a per-block staking rate limit. The legacy StakingRateLimitExceeded error remains but is not enforced in the current code. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RaoFoundation/subtensor/main/pallets/subtensor/src/staking/stake_utils.rs
open_questions: Will governance raise SubnetLimit above 128? The v440 commit message says 'subnet limit 256', but on-chain it is 128 and the v440 release page says the increase is deferred. A higher cap would change prune frequency and slot value.

MinerBurned scaling was removed in v444 (2026-08-06) and restored in #3071 (2026-08-12). EmissionBarRank, EmissionGateExponent and SubnetMovingAlpha are all set by root/governance and have changed recently. How stable are they? Monitor on-chain values instead of hardcoding them.

When and on what criteria does governance flip SubnetEmissionEnabled for newly registered subnets? SN36 has been disabled for about 49 days while others of similar age are enabled. This sets when a new micro-cap starts receiving TAO injection.

How large and how frequent are basket-driven flows: staker claims selling alpha pro-rata, and validator swap_basket trades under the 10%-of-NAV/day budget? These replaced per-block root selling. Claim timing is discretionary, so this sell pressure is lumpy.

Exact mainnet activation block of the Balancer (palswap) migration from Swap V3. The commits date from Jan–May 2026; I did not pin the deployment block, which matters for backtests that need V3-era tick math.
Exact extrinsic transaction fees (weight fees) for add_stake_limit and remove_stake_limit on mainnet. These need payment_queryInfo on a signed extrinsic or a btcli --dry-run. I did not measure them.

Null Consensus (labelled 'Upcoming' on the releases page, though code merged around spec 474) changes how miner incentives and dividends are distributed within subnets that opt in. Its effect on alpha sell flow is unknown.
The on-chain BasketConcentrationCap is raw value 7,865 (about 12% if it is u16/65535). The docs say 1/16 at launch. I did not verify the encoding and units.

The deregistration haircut estimates use SubnetAlphaOut as a stand-in for the sum of staker alpha. Exact payouts also depend on how much the AMM sale of validator basket holdings drains the pool before distribution. Treat the 35–65% haircut as an estimate.
Taostats and tao.app data provider APIs (endpoints, history depth, whether they expose the moving price, MinerBurned and emission-gate fields) were not covered here.

summary:
The Python tooling has changed a lot since mid-2026. The opentensor/bittensor repo was archived on 2026-07-10. Since bittensor 11.0.0 (PyPI, 2026-07-17) the SDK has lived in the subtensor monorepo at github.com/RaoFoundation/subtensor/sdk/python. Requests to github.com/opentensor/subtensor now 301-redirect there. The latest release is bittensor 11.3.0 (2026-10-07), which needs Python 3.10–3.14 and bundles btcli and the wallet. That means the separate bittensor-cli and bittensor-wallet packages are no longer needed. docs.learnbittensor.org 301-redirects to bittensor.com/docs. v11 dropped the v10 method-per-operation API (subtensor.add_stake, unstake, AsyncSubtensor). A write is now an Intent object (bt.AddStake, bt.RemoveStakeLimit, bt.SwapStake, bt.MoveStake, ...). You preview it with client.plan() and submit it with client.execute() or client.submit_shielded(). An optional bt.Policy can cap spend and restrict which netuids are allowed. In v11, AddStake, RemoveStake, SwapStake and cross-subnet MoveStake have slippage protection on by default with a 5% tolerance, built as *_limit extrinsics with allow_partial=False. The SDK execute() does NOT MEV-shield automatically; you must call submit_shielded(). The last v10 release is 10.5.0 (2026-06-25). There, safe_staking defaults to False, rate_tolerance to 0.005, and mev_protection is read from the BT_MEV_PROTECTION environment variable (default off).

On chain, mainnet runs spec_version 475 (Runtime 475 released 2026-10-07; v476 was proposed on 2026-10-08). Runtime releases are close to daily. Every subnet pool is a weighted Balancer AMM: price = w1·TAO / (w2·alpha). A live check found all 128 pools at weights of about 0.5, so the reserve ratio currently equals spot. The default swap fee is 33/65535 (about 0.05%). It comes off the input and goes to the block author. Limit prices are in rao per alpha (price × 1e9) and bound the pool's marginal spot price after the fill, not the average fill price. SwapRuntimeApi (current_alpha_price, current_alpha_price_all, sim_swap_tao_for_alpha, sim_swap_alpha_for_tao) runs the same swap path as execution, so its quotes are exact. On failure it returns all zeros rather than an error. In current source there is no per-block staking rate limit and no stake/unstake cooldown, and there is no unbonding period. The StakingRateLimitExceeded error is still declared but never raised. The only time locks are opt-in conviction locks and a root-only RootStakeUnlockInterval, which is currently 0 on mainnet. Other rules: the minimum stake is 0.002 TAO plus the fee, a partial unstake must leave at least 0.002 TAO worth behind, and a single swap may not exceed 1000× the pool's TAO reserve.

The MEV Shield is live on mainnet. It is an ML-KEM-768 + XChaCha20-Poly1305 encrypted mempool through MevShield.submit_encrypted, and the carrier transaction must use an era of 8 blocks or less. Tips do not raise priority. For bot security, pallet_proxy ProxyType::Staking (index 8) allows add, remove, move and swap stake plus the limit variants and unstake_all. It does not allow balance transfers, transfer_stake or Utility.batch_all. The official docs warn that a leaked zero-delay Staking proxy can still drain value through high-slippage round trips. That risk is real for micro-cap pools. In v11 you use a proxy with execute(intent, delegate_wallet, proxy_for=<real coldkey>, proxy_type="Staking"), and shielding composes with the proxy wrapper. Public RPC is about 1 request per second per IP. For anything serious, run your own lite node (about 128 GB, warp sync); historical reads beyond about 300 blocks need an archive node. Live liquidity at block ~9.24M (2026-10-08): TAO reserves range from 241 TAO (minimum) to about 2,944 (25th percentile), about 6,723 (median) and about 202k (maximum). A 10 TAO buy in the thinnest pool costs about 4.1% on average and moves spot about 8.5%.

findings.claim: The Python SDK moved and had a major version change. opentensor/bittensor is archived. bittensor v11 is developed in the RaoFoundation/subtensor monorepo. The current PyPI release is 11.3.0 (2026-10-07).
findings.detail: opentensor/bittensor README: 'archived by the owner on Jul 10, 2026' and 'SDK development moved to the subtensor monorepo' (github.com/RaoFoundation/subtensor, sdk/python). No further releases come from the old repo. PyPI release dates: 10.4.0 2026-05-28, 10.4.1 2026-06-11, 10.5.0 2026-06-25 (last v10), 11.0.0 2026-07-17, 11.0.1 2026-07-23, 11.0.2 2026-08-03, 11.1.0 2026-08-14, 11.3.0 2026-10-07 (no 11.2.0 final). requires_python is '>=3.10,<3.15'. v11 ships `import bittensor` and the `btcli` CLI and replaces the bittensor-cli package (last 9.23.2, 2026-07-12) and the bittensor-wallet package (last 4.1.1, 2026-07-12). v11 has no axon/dendrite/synapse. github.com/opentensor/subtensor returns 301 to github.com/RaoFoundation/subtensor (same repo, created 2023). docs.learnbittensor.org/* returns 301 to bittensor.com/docs. Install: pip install bittensor==11.3.0.

verification.evidence: PyPI JSON shows version 11.3.0 (uploaded 2026-10-07T22:56Z) with requires_python '<3.15,>=3.10'. Project URLs point to bittensor.com/docs and github.com/RaoFoundation/subtensor. Final upload dates: 10.4.0 05-28, 10.4.1 06-11, 10.5.0 06-25, 11.0.0 07-17, 11.0.1 07-23, 11.0.2 08-03, 11.1.0 08-14, 11.3.0 10-07. Only 11.2.0rc34 exists, with no 11.2.0 final. bittensor-cli's last release is 9.23.2 (07-12) and bittensor-wallet's is 4.1.1 (07-12). The GitHub API reports opentensor/bittensor as archived (pushed_at 2026-07-10). Its README says it is archived and that development moved to RaoFoundation/subtensor sdk/python as Bittensor 11. bittensor/__init__.py raises a removal hint for axon, dendrite and Synapse. opentensor/subtensor returns 301 to RaoFoundation/subtensor (created 2023-03-02). docs.learnbittensor.org returns 301 to https://bittensor.com/docs. Nuance: opentensor/bittensor itself now resolves to RaoFoundation/bittensor, and v11 still has a ServeAxon intent for publishing an endpoint.

findings.claim: v11 removed the v10 Subtensor/AsyncSubtensor staking methods. Every write is now an Intent dataclass submitted with client.plan, client.execute or client.submit_shielded.
findings.detail: bt.Subtensor() is a blocking client that connects lazily and is the default for finney. Async use: `async with bt.Subtensor(net) as client:` or `client = await bt.Subtensor(net)`. Accessing bt.AsyncSubtensor, get_async_subtensor or MockSubtensor raises an error with a migration hint. bt.subtensor and bt.wallet are lowercase aliases. Migration map (docs/migration): add_stake(...) -> bt.AddStake(hotkey_ss58, netuid, amount_tao). add_stake(safe_staking=True, rate_tolerance) -> bt.AddStakeLimit(..., limit_price_rao, allow_partial). unstake -> bt.RemoveStake(hotkey_ss58, netuid, amount_alpha), which accepts 'all'. unstake(safe_unstaking=True) -> bt.RemoveStakeLimit. unstake_all -> bt.UnstakeAll(hotkey_ss58) or bt.UnstakeAllAlpha. swap_stake -> bt.SwapStake(hotkey_ss58, origin_netuid, dest_netuid, amount_alpha). move_stake -> bt.MoveStake(origin_hotkey_ss58, origin_netuid, dest_hotkey_ss58, dest_netuid, amount_alpha). transfer_stake -> bt.TransferStake(dest_coldkey_ss58, hotkey_ss58, origin_netuid, dest_netuid, amount_alpha). period becomes a keyword of execute. The allow_partial_stake config key has no equivalent.

verification.evidence: In __init__.py, Subtensor is exported with lowercase aliases subtensor and wallet. A __getattr__ removal map covers AsyncSubtensor, async_subtensor, get_async_subtensor and MockSubtensor, and links to /docs/migration. migration.mdx has the same intent mapping table, including the period/wait kwargs moving to execute(). It also states that the rate_tolerance, safe_staking and allow_partial_stake config keys have no equivalent.

findings.claim: Exact v11 staking intent fields and defaults. AddStake, RemoveStake, SwapStake and cross-subnet MoveStake have slippage protection ON by default with rate_tolerance=0.05, compiled to *_limit extrinsics with allow_partial=False.
findings.detail:
From intents/staking.py (DEFAULT_RATE_TOLERANCE = 0.05; rate_tolerance must be in [0, 1)):
- AddStake(hotkey_ss58: str, netuid: int, amount_tao: Money|'all', slippage_protection=True, rate_tolerance=0.05). Builds add_stake_limit(limit_price=int(spot_rao*(1+tol)), allow_partial=False), or plain add_stake if protection is off. 'all' means free balance minus existential deposit minus 500,000 rao of fee headroom.
- RemoveStake(hotkey_ss58, netuid, amount_alpha|'all', slippage_protection=True, rate_tolerance=0.05, claim=False). Builds remove_stake_limit(limit=int(spot*(1-tol)), allow_partial=False).
- AddStakeLimit(hotkey_ss58, netuid, amount_tao, limit_price_rao: int, allow_partial=False).
- RemoveStakeLimit(hotkey_ss58, netuid, amount_alpha, limit_price_rao: int, allow_partial=False, claim=False).
- UnstakeAll(hotkey_ss58, claim=False) unstakes every subnet including root, with NO price limit, and silently skips positions that fail. UnstakeAllAlpha(hotkey_ss58) sells all alpha into root stake, also with no limit.
- SwapStake(hotkey_ss58, origin_netuid, dest_netuid, amount_alpha, slippage_protection=True, rate_tolerance=0.05). Uses swap_stake_limit with limit = (origin_price*1e9 // dest_price)*(1-tol).
- MoveStake(origin_hotkey_ss58, origin_netuid, dest_hotkey_ss58, dest_netuid, amount_alpha, slippage_protection=True, rate_tolerance=0.05, claim=False). A same-subnet move is a fee-free plain move_stake with no swap.
- MoveSwapStake(...) wraps Utility.batch_all [move_stake, swap_stake_limit]. It moves amount-1 rao because of share-pool rounding.
- TransferStake(dest_coldkey_ss58, hotkey_ss58, origin_netuid, dest_netuid, amount_alpha, dest_hotkey_ss58=None). This changes the owner irreversibly and gets TransferDisallowed if the subnet owner disabled transfers.
Every staking intent has mev_shield_default=True, but that flag only drives the CLI default.

verification.correction: Most fields and defaults are right. Two details need fixing. (1) A same-subnet MoveStake has no swap and no swap fee, but it is not fee-free. move_stake is declared Pays::Yes, and migration.mdx says 'Same-subnet move_stake is not a pool swap, but it is not fee-free.' (2) MoveSwapStake moves the FULL amount with move_stake and then swaps amount-1 rao with swap_stake_limit, leaving 1 rao of dust on the destination hotkey at the origin subnet. It does not move amount-1. MoveSwapStake also refuses origin_hotkey == dest_hotkey. The docs now prefer MoveStake, which compiles a cross-subnet move into a single move_stake_limit (runtime v448+).
verification.evidence: intents/staking.py: DEFAULT_RATE_TOLERANCE = 0.05. _check_rate_tolerance enforces 0 <= tol < 1. AddStake builds add_stake_limit with limit_price=int(price*(1+tol)) and allow_partial=False. RemoveStake uses int(price*(1-tol)). _swap_limit_price_rao = int((origin_price*RAO_PER_TAO//dest_price)*(1-tol)). _ALL_STAKE_FEE_HEADROOM_RAO = 500_000, and 'all' = free - ExistentialDeposit - headroom. UnstakeAll and UnstakeAllAlpha have no price limit and silently skip failing positions. _compose_move_then_swap does move_stake(rao) then swap of _executable_after_same_subnet_move(rao) = rao-1. dispatches.rs move_stake is Pays::Yes.

findings.claim: v11 Executor signatures. execute() submits in the clear and waits for finalization by default. MEV protection requires an explicit submit_shielded().
findings.detail:
execute(intent, wallet, *, policy=None, proxy_for=None, proxy_type=None, period=DEFAULT_ERA_PERIOD(128), wait_for_inclusion=True, wait_for_finalization=True, retries=0, wait_for_registration=True, registration_timeout=None, on_progress=None) -> ExtrinsicResult.
submit_shielded(intent, wallet, *, policy=None, proxy_for=None, proxy_type=None, period=MEV_SHIELD_ERA_PERIOD(8), wait_for_inclusion=True, wait_for_finalization=False, ...).
