findings.claim: The current emission regime (since 2026-06-22, gated since v440 in July 2026) starves micro caps. Shares follow EMA price × (1 − MinerBurned) passed through a Hill gate centred at rank 32, so on-chain the top 32 subnets receive 97% of the TAO entering pools and the bottom third by pool size gets a median of 0 TAO/day.
findings.detail:
How the share is computed (code get_shares):
- price_share_i = SubnetMovingPrice_i / Σ moving prices.
- That share is multiplied by (1 − MinerBurned_i) and renormalised.
- The gate is gate = 1/(1+(θ/s)^h), with θ set by EmissionBarRank (default 32, rank mode) and h = EmissionGateExponent (default 3). θ is recomputed every EMISSION_BAR_UPDATE_INTERVAL=360 blocks.
- Live EmissionGateBar θ = 0.00826 (an 0.83% share). EmissionBarQuantile is stored as 0.75 but is inactive while rank > 0.
- Subnets with SubnetEmissionEnabled=false have their share redistributed.

What a subnet keeps at a given share s:
| s | Gate kept |
|---|---|
| θ | 50% |
| θ/2 | 11% |
| θ/3 | 3.6% |
| θ/5 | 0.8% |

The official v440 snapshot (126 subnets, July 2026):
- The 94 subnets below the bar fell from 38.4% to 12.5% of emission; the top 8 rose from 32.8% to 52.7%.
- 80% of emission is reached by rank 23 (previously 64); the effective number of subnets fell from about 50 to about 22.

Live per-block storage (SubnetTaoInEmission + SubnetExcessTao) sums to exactly 0.5 TAO/block = 3,600 TAO/day. Of that, 1,131 TAO/day is direct tao_in and 2,468 TAO/day is protocol chain buys (the injection is capped at RootProp × alpha emission; RootProp ranges 0.133–0.879, median 0.157).

Concentration: top 8 get 53.2%, top 16 76.3%, top 32 97.2%, top 48 99.7%. Only 50 subnets get at least 1 TAO/day and 35 get at least 10 TAO/day. By pool-size tercile, median TAO/day received is 0 (bottom, sum 140), 0.17 (middle), 29.35 (top).

Top recipients (TAO/day): SN51 471, SN64 329, SN4 243, SN120 214, SN107 180.

Emission tracks price rank, not pool depth. A small pool with a high EMA price, such as SN90 (pool 4,050 TAO, price 0.0212), can receive a large daily injection relative to its pool.
sources: on-chain SubnetTaoInEmission, SubnetExcessTao, EmissionGateBar, RootProp via https://entrypoint-finney.opentensor.ai block ~9,240,500

findings.claim: Every started subnet mints 1 alpha per block (7,200/day) whatever its TAO emission, including subnets with emission disabled. Micro caps that receive no TAO injection therefore carry continuous dilution and sell pressure.
findings.detail:
On-chain SubnetAlphaOutEmission takes only the values {0.0, 1.0} alpha/block: 0 for subnets not yet started, 1.0 for everything else. That includes the emission-disabled SN29, SN35, SN36, SN108 and SN116.

Per-tempo split: owner 18% (SubnetOwnerCut 11796/65535), miners 41%, validators/stakers 41%. Miners therefore receive about 2,952 alpha/day per subnet (the chainbuying screener uses the same figure).

Example: a micro cap with a 1,000–2,000 TAO pool at a price of 0.002–0.004 TAO emits about 6–12 TAO/day of miner alpha. That is roughly 0.4–1.2% of the pool per day if sold, against a median of 0 TAO/day of injection.

The docs say disabling emission zeroes only the pool-side alpha_in/tao_in/chain-buy paths, not alpha_out or the owner cut.

Offsets: MinerBurned (27 subnets currently burn at least 99% of miner emission; 64 burn a non-zero share) and Conviction auto-lock of owner emissions (see D12). Alpha issuance halves per subnet at 10.5M alpha issued (FalconX, secondary); the oldest subnets may reach that in 2027.
sources: on-chain SubtensorModule.SubnetAlphaOutEmission, SubnetEmissionEnabled, FirstEmissionBlockNumber, MinerBurned via https://entrypoint-finney.opentensor.ai block 9,240,571

The largest issuances are now ~6.4M (SN4 6.41M, SN64 6.39M, SN12 6.38M) and grow by ~7,200–8,200/day, so the first halvings are more likely ~early 2028 than 2027. - Lifespan median 317 days (min 128, max 835).

- Many had 90-day log returns between −0.4 and −3.05.

The rule (root.rs get_network_to_prune): the lowest get_moving_alpha_price among added, non-root subnets past immunity; ties go to the earliest registration.

Live prune order at block 9,240,571: SN92 (EMA 0.00136), SN47 (0.0017), SN72, SN42, SN55, SN65. SN16 (EMA 0.00095) leaves immunity in about 84k blocks (~2026-10-20), and SN99 (0.001) in about 27 days.

sources: own computation via https://bittensor-finney.api.onfinality.io/public (NetworkRegisteredAt, SubnetTAO, SubnetAlphaIn, SubnetAlphaOut)

verification.correction:
SN90 is not top-10 by emission. On-chain TAO injection ranks it 14th (96 TAO/day, 2.67%). SN107 is 5th (180 TAO/day, 5.0%). The prune order also misses subnets that have never started: their SubnetMovingPrice is 0, so they become the first prune candidates once immune.

- SN82: ~779k blocks.

Pruning happens only inside do_register_network, and at most one registration is allowed per NetworkRateLimit (14,400 blocks) network-wide. When the network is full, the new registration is queued behind multi-block dissolution (NetworkRegistrationQueue/DissolveCleanupQueue).
verification.evidence:
get_network_to_prune iterates NetworksAdded, skips root and immune subnets (current_block < reg + NetworkImmunityPeriod), and picks the minimum get_moving_alpha_price with the earliest registration on ties. Confirmed. Live order at block 9,240,605: SN92 0.00136, SN47 0.00170, SN72 0.00205, SN42 0.00207, SN55 0.00210, SN65 0.00214, then SN98 and SN127. SN16 leaves immunity in 84,041 blocks; SN99 in 195,451.

Current NetworkRegisteredAt values match the researcher's dates. Examples: SN116 9,210,632 = 2026-10-04; SN92 8,352,006; SN16 8,460,646 = 2026-06-22; SN90 8,618,670 = 2026-07-14; SN47 = 2026-01-17; SN107 = 2026-02-02. 42 current netuids were registered since ~2025-10-19, which equals 52 events minus 10 repeat netuids in the researcher's list.

findings.claim: What holders receive on deregistration: the pool's SubnetTAO is paid pro rata to coldkey free balance. For legacy subnets this is roughly 0.45–1.0× spot. For subnets registered after block 8,334,450 (~2026-06-04), the pool's own alpha also counts in the denominator, cutting recovery to roughly 0.3–0.5× spot. Owner lock refunds apply only to legacy subnets.
findings.detail:
How the payout is computed (remove_stake.rs, destroy_alpha_in_out_stakes_*):
- pot_tao = SubnetTAO.
- share = pot × alpha_value_i / total_alpha_value; dust is allocated by largest remainder.
- total_alpha_value = Σ holders' share-pool values + protocol alpha.
- For subnets with reg_at > TaoInRefundDeploymentBlock (on-chain 8,334,450), SubnetAlphaIn + SubnetProtocolAlpha are added to the denominator. Comment: 'Legacy subnets keep the old dereg behavior: ignore SubnetAlphaIn.'
- Payout goes to coldkey free balance via transfer_tao_from_subnet; it is not restaked.

Approximate recovery per alpha relative to spot (T/alpha_in):
- Legacy: ≈ alpha_in/alpha_out. The observed pre-prune range was 0.45–1.03.
- New: ≈ alpha_in/(alpha_in + alpha_out + protocol).
- Example: SN92 now has pool 587 TAO, alpha_in about 435k, alpha_out 632k, giving about 0.41× spot.

Owner refund: should_refund_owner = reg_at < start_block. Refund = lock_cost − owner_emission_tao (owner alpha valued at the current price), capped by what is transferable, plus any leftover pot. Newer subnets' locks go entirely into the pool and are not refunded.

Conviction/decaying locks and basket holdings are cleared in later phases (dissolution.rs). The docs mention up to 96.875% loss in adverse cases (secondary, worst case).

verification.correction:
Three fixes:
1. Chain-buy alpha is added to SubnetAlphaOut when bought (swap_tao_for_alpha mutates SubnetAlphaOut; run_coinbase also adds it to SubnetProtocolAlpha). So Σholders + protocol ≈ AlphaOut, and the stated new-subnet recovery 'alpha_in/(alpha_in+alpha_out+protocol)' double-counts. The right approximation is ≈ alpha_in/(alpha_in+alpha_out); legacy subnets ≈ alpha_in/alpha_out. For SN92 (pool 585 TAO, alpha_in 437,016, alpha_out 630,791, protocol 41,187) that gives 0.41x. The researcher's 0.41 matches the corrected formula; the stated one gives 0.39.
2. The pot share for alpha_in + protocol alpha is not paid to holders. It is recycled, or refunded to the owner on legacy subnets.
3. The owner-refund 'legacy' threshold is a different block. should_refund_owner = reg_at < NetworkRegistrationStartBlock = 6,573,966 (2025-10-02). TaoInRefundDeploymentBlock = 8,334,450 (2026-06-04 16:49 UTC) is the threshold for the denominator.
verification.evidence: remove_stake.rs destroy_alpha_in_out_stakes_get_total_alpha_value: if reg_at > TaoInRefundDeploymentBlock, the base is SubnetAlphaIn + SubnetProtocolAlpha, else SubnetProtocolAlpha ('Legacy subnets keep the old dereg behavior: ignore SubnetAlphaIn'). The settle phase distributes pot*alpha_val/total by largest remainder via transfer_tao_from_subnet to the coldkey. destroy_alpha_in_out_stakes computes refund = lock_cost - owner_emission_tao, priced at current_alpha_price, only if reg_at < NetworkRegistrationStartBlock. The remaining subnet balance is recycled. On-chain NetworkRegistrationStartBlock=6,573,966 and TaoInRefundDeploymentBlock=8,334,450. dissolution.rs defines the multi-phase cleanup (locks and decaying locks phases 2.5–2.6). The 96.875% docs figure is not verified.

findings.claim: New-subnet launch dynamics changed by regime. Feb–Sep 2025 tiny-pool launches were sniped hard and then decayed about 99%. Oct 2025 – Apr 2026 launches started with near-empty pools. Since late April 2026, new pools are seeded with the full lock (~900–1,300 TAO) at the network-median price, show little sniping, and drift down about 74% by day 90.
findings.detail:
Current mechanics (subnet.rs set_new_network_state):
- SubnetTAO = the lock paid (1–1,300+ TAO recently).
- SubnetAlphaIn = lock / median_subnet_alpha_price; SubnetAlphaOut = 0.
- SubnetEmissionEnabled is set to false at registration and only root can enable it.
- do_start_call sets FirstEmissionBlockNumber and SubtokenEnabled.
- Hotfix v3.3.15-402 (May 8, 2026, PR #2649) set owner_alpha_stake = 0. Before that, owners got free alpha = (lock − floor)/median price.
- The EMA price starts at 0 and warms up (ema_alpha scales with blocks_since_start/(blocks_since_start + 201,600)). That, plus the disabled flag and the rank-32 gate, means new subnets get almost no TAO emission for weeks while minting 1 alpha/block once started.

My on-chain launch cohorts (price path measured from the first day the price moved):

A: Feb–Sep 2025 (n=65)
- Pool at first move: median 4 TAO.
- 14-day max run-up: median +44%, 75th percentile +164%, max +1,742%. Secondary (TAO Times, May 2025): TAOHash +10,200%.
- Path: day 30 −72%, day 90 −83%, day 180 −99.9%; only 18% positive at day 180.
- Pools grew to 248 TAO by day 30 and 899 by day 90.

B: Oct 2025 – Apr 2026 (n=30)
- About 7 days from registration to first move; pools started near 0 TAO (a 2,500 TAO burn rather than a pool seed).
- Path: day 7 −31%, day 30 −29%, day 90 −28%, day 180 −58%.
- Pools reached 348 TAO by day 30 and 1,399 by day 90.

C: since Apr 25, 2026, full-lock seeding (n=21)
- Pool at start: median 1,227 TAO.
- 14-day max run-up: median +9%, 75th percentile +23%, max +132%.
- Path: day 7 −7.7%, day 14 −11.6%, day 30 −25% (14% positive), day 60 −66%, day 90 −74% (n=11, 0% positive).
- Pools: 1,860 TAO at day 30, 1,529 at day 90.

The right tail exists but is rare: SN90 re-registered on Jul 15, 2026 and reached the top 10 by emission within about 3 months.

I found no on-chain study of first-block sniping bots; evidence of bot sniping is anecdotal or vendor marketing (e.g. FlowSniper).

verification.correction:
The mechanics are confirmed. My replication of cohort C (registered after ~2026-04-25, n=21, path measured from the first daily price move) gives:
- Median pool at first move ~1,004 TAO (not 1,227); median 14-day max run-up +6.2%.
- Day 7 and day 14 medians 0.0% (60% positive); day 30 -4.7% (n=18, 50% positive).
- Day 60 -57.7% (n=14, 29% positive); day 90 -68.3% (n=11, 0% positive).
So the 90-day decline holds (about -68% vs -74%), but the first month is much flatter than the claimed -25%/14% positive, and the result is sensitive to how 'first move' is defined.

EMA warm-up: with on-chain SubnetMovingAlpha=0.0003, the EMA reaches ~80% of spot about 7 days after start and ~100% after ~14 days. The lack of emission for new subnets comes mainly from SubnetEmissionEnabled=false and the gate, not the EMA.
verification.evidence: subnet.rs set_new_network_state: SubnetTAO = actual lock; SubnetAlphaIn = lock/median_subnet_alpha_price; SubnetAlphaOut = 0; no owner alpha stake; '--- 10. Default emission off' writes SubnetEmissionEnabled=false. do_start_call sets FirstEmissionBlockNumber = now+1 and SubtokenEnabled, subject to StartCallDelay (0). PR #2649 'Hotfix to remove initial owners alpha' merged 2026-05-08; PR #2642 'No initial owner alpha' merged 2026-05-06. stake_utils.rs update_moving_price: alpha = SubnetMovingAlpha * b/(b + EMAPriceHalvingBlocks), with default 201,600 (all netuids null, so default). Spot input is clamped at 1.0. Cohort A/B figures were not checked.

findings.claim: Owner dumping: Covenant AI's exit (Apr 9–10, 2026) is the defining incident. About 37k TAO of alpha was sold across SN3/SN39/SN81, those subnets fell up to 40% immediately, and TAO fell about 20–27%. The protocol responded with Conviction locks (May 13, 2026), removal of owner registration alpha (May 8), and an 18% ownership gate (v447, Aug 2026).
findings.detail:
FalconX (May 13, 2026, secondary): Covenant ran Templar SN3, Basilica SN39 and Grail SN81, three of the top 15 by market cap. It 'sold all of its subnet tokens'; affected prices fell up to 40% almost instantly and TAO fell 24% within hours.

Other coverage (secondary):
- About 37,000 TAO (~$10M) of alpha sold.
- TAO went from about $332–340 to a low of about $253–264, with about $9M of longs liquidated.
- Attribution is disputed: Const said he sold under 1% of his own holdings on those near-100%-burn subnets.

Conviction (secondary, tao.media May 8, 2026; PRs #2599/#2632/#2641/#2642):
- Owner emissions are auto-locked on arrival.
- An unlock is a public transaction; about 63% is spendable after ~30 days and 95% after ~90 days (exponential decay).
- Phase 2 will add owner elections by locked conviction.
- v439 (July 2026) added owner-cut auto-lock controls. A FalconX-era source says owner_cut_auto_lock_enabled was off by default; this conflicts and should be verified on-chain.
- v447 (Aug 2026): ownership gate at an 18% conviction threshold.

Structural note: under Taoflow, owners and miners selling the 18%/41% alpha cuts were recorded as outflows. Taostats (Apr 16, 2026, via FalconX) showed 67 of 128 subnets burning at least 99% of incentives, i.e. withholding miner emission to avoid outflows. Live today: 27 subnets with MinerBurned ≥ 0.99, which now directly cuts their emission share.

verification.correction:
The Conviction details come from the May 2026 launch coverage and are outdated:
- Unlock decay is now locked_mass*exp(-dt/UnlockRate) with UnlockRate default 934,866 blocks (on-chain null, so default; code comment '50% lock back in ~90 days'). That is ~21% unlocked after 30 days and 50% after 90 days, not 63%/95%. MaturityRate on-chain is 311,622.
- Owner emissions are NOT auto-locked by default. OwnerCutAutoLockEnabled defaults to false, and only 13 subnets have it on: 17, 31, 34, 51, 53, 64, 73, 87, 90, 96, 106, 109, 122.
- The v447 ownership gate reassigns ownership only if the subnet is at least ONE_YEAR (7200*365+1800 blocks) old AND a single hotkey's conviction exceeds 18% of (SubnetAlphaOut - SubnetProtocolAlpha - AlphaBurned).
- Conviction PRs were merged: #2599 2026-05-01, #2632 05-05, #2641 05-06, #2642 05-06; tao.media said the auto-lock took effect May 13.
The Covenant facts stand: FalconX (May 13, 2026) says it 'sold all its subnet tokens', subnets fell up to 40%, TAO fell 24%. cryptotimes reports ~37,000 TAO alleged, $332 to $254, and over $9M of longs liquidated. Const's '<1%' statement was not verified.
verification.evidence: lib.rs DefaultOwnerCutAutoLockEnabled=false ('auto-locking is disabled unless explicitly enabled'); DefaultUnlockRate=934_866; DefaultMaturityRate=934_866. lock.rs calculate_decayed_mass_and_conviction uses exp_decay(dt, unlock_rate); change_subnet_owner_if_needed is documented with the 1-year and 18% single-hotkey gate. On-chain reads of OwnerCutAutoLockEnabled, UnlockRate and MaturityRate. tao.media (May 8, 2026) is the source of the 63%/95% and auto-lock claims. FalconX gives 67/128 burning at least 99% (Taostats, Apr 16). Live MinerBurned is at least 0.99 on 27 subnets.

findings.claim: Taoflow (Nov 2025 – Jun 21, 2026) allocated emission by net staking flow, with a 30-day-half-life EMA and zero emission for negative flow. That favoured small subnets with inflows (SMB +0.58%/day) and zeroed even the largest pools. It was replaced on 2026-06-22 and the code is now dead.
findings.detail:
Code (now #[allow(dead_code)] get_shares_flow):
- SubnetTaoFlow is a signed accumulator: stake adds, unstake subtracts.
- EMA with FlowEmaSmoothingFactor = 29,597,889,189,277/i64::MAX ≈ 3.209e-6 per block (FlowHalfLife 216,000 blocks ≈ 30 days).
- Optional net mode subtracts protocol flow scaled by the ratio of user to protocol positive sums.
- Offset L = max{TaoFlowCutoff, min(min S_i, 0)}; z_i = max(S_i − L, 0); shares = z_i^p / Σ z^p (FlowNormExponent p).

Effects:
- Kucoin/Vadim (Apr 15, 2026, secondary): SN64 Chutes ($64.6M pool) and SN4 Targon ($37.0M) got $0/day emission, while SN97's $582K pool got about $47K/day (about 8% of its pool per day). SN64's flow went from −107 to −135 within four hours.
- Maymin notes Taoflow's start coincided with the Dec 2025 halving, so the two effects cannot be separated.
- The June 2026 purge targeted 'TaoFlow exploiters' among other abuses (secondary). I found no documented, quantified wash-flow incident.

Transition: activated around Nov 5, 2025 with a 30-day ramp (SimplyTao, secondary). Messari logs a Nov 5, 2025 release that re-enabled flow tracking. PR #2781 (hotfix, merged 2026-06-22) moved shares to price EMA × (1 − MinerBurned).

verification.evidence:
subnet_emissions.rs has get_shares_flow, get_ema_flow and get_lower_limit marked #[allow(dead_code)]; get_shares uses price EMA only.
- EMA flow: (1-a)*last + a*block_flow, with a = FlowEmaSmoothingFactor/i64::MAX. The default 29,597,889,189,277 equals 3.209e-6, and FlowHalfLife is 216,000.
- L = max(TaoFlowCutoff, min(min S_i, 0)), with DefaultFlowCutoff=0 (null on-chain at blocks 6.7M, 7.9M and 9.24M). So negative-flow subnets got z=0.
- Net mode: norm = min(1, user_pos_sum/protocol_pos_sum), applied only to positive protocol EMA. NetTaoFlowEnabled default true; FlowNormExponent default 1.
- PR #2781 merged 2026-06-22.
The Kucoin/SimplyTao/Messari details are secondary and unchecked.

findings.claim: Emission kill switches and purges are a live regime risk. On 2026-06-22, 57 of 128 subnets had emissions halted (no active miner distribution or no code), with weekly Monday reviews. New subnets start with SubnetEmissionEnabled=false until root enables them, and 6 subnets are disabled today.
findings.detail:
Ourcryptotalk (Jun 23, 2026, secondary):
- Const posted on Discord around 16:26 UTC on Jun 22.
- 57/128 subnets (~45%) were halted and about 3,600 TAO/day redirected.
- Named targets: 100% miner burn without launch plans, self-mining via stake weight, abandoned subnets, 'TaoFlow exploiters'.
- Reinstatement is case by case at weekly Monday reviews.

Hackernoon (Jul 8, 2026, secondary): more than 50 subnets lost weekly emissions.

Mechanism: root-only SubnetEmissionEnabled. Disabling it zeroes tao_in/alpha_in/chain-buy paths, but alpha_out and the owner cut continue.

Live disabled set (block 9,240,571): SN29 (old), SN35, SN36, SN82, SN108, SN116 (recent registrations).

CoinMarketCap (Jun 24, 2026): TAO around $214–223; no single headline drove the move.

Root Reborn snapshot (Jul 24, 2026): 'Subnets live: 89 of 128'.

verification.correction: Nit: ourcryptotalk puts TAO at $230–238 over June 20–23, which conflicts with the cited CMC $214–223. The newest live state shows that some disabled subnets are older (SN29) and some have never started (SN82).
verification.evidence: ourcryptotalk (Jun 23, 2026): 57 of 128 halted; Const's Discord post ~16:26 UTC Jun 22; ~3,600 TAO/day redirected; weekly Monday reviews; the criteria match. Code: SubnetEmissionEnabled is root-set; registration writes false. The live disabled set at block 9,240,605 is exactly SN29, SN35, SN36, SN82, SN108, SN116. The v441 page shows 'Subnets live and earning 89 of 128'.

findings.claim: MEV and sandwiching: sandwich bots on add/remove_stake were a top complaint in 2025. Slippage-limit extrinsics blocked most of it, and MEV Shield (encrypted mempool, ML-KEM-768) went live around 2025-12-24 and is the default in btcli/SDK for sensitive coldkey operations.
findings.detail:
Background:
- Taostats (Dec 12, 2025) says slippage limits stopped most sandwiching but large trades still leaked value.
- Macrocosmos sentiment study (Nov 2025, 49,799 posts): subnet owners called MEV bots the '#1 thing we hate in dTAO', especially around buybacks.
- The OTF X post announcing MEV Shield is dated 2025-12-24 (decoded from the post ID).

Controls:
- AddStakeLimit/RemoveStakeLimit take limit_price_rao: ceiling = spot × (1 + tol) for buys, floor = spot × (1 − tol) for sells.
- allow_partial=false rejects the whole order if the limit is hit.
- Plain remove_stake has no price limit.
- SDK: client.submit_shielded(...) encrypts to the chain's rotating ML-KEM-768 key. Kucoin describes the flag as mev_protection=True.
- Shielding fails for hotkey-signed extrinsics, and adds nothing for swaps well under ~1 TAO.

Residual risk: shielding hides intent only while a transaction is pending. Bots can still react to state after inclusion (e.g. after start_call or large flows). This is my inference.

verification.correction: In SDK v11, shielding is NOT the default for Client.execute(). Only intents with mev_shield_required (e.g. collateral buys) are redirected to submit_shielded. mev_shield_default=True on AddStake, AddStakeLimit and similar is a btcli default, toggled with --mev-shield/--no-mev-shield. A Python algo must call `await client.submit_shielded(intent, wallet, ...)` explicitly. Separately, the SDK AddStake intent is itself slippage-protected by default: rate_tolerance 0.05, composed as add_stake_limit with allow_partial=False.
verification.evidence: intents/base.py comment: 'Whether the CLI submits this intent MEV-shielded by default'. executor.py execute() redirects only when mev_shield_required. submit_shielded docstring: encrypted 'with the chain's rotating ML-KEM-768 key (NextKey)' and carried in MevShield.submit_encrypted; ciphertext max 8192 bytes; mortal era MEV_SHIELD_ERA_PERIOD. learnbittensor docs: hotkey-signed extrinsics are not supported. X post IDs decode to 2025-12-24T20:00Z (opentensor) and 2025-12-12 (taostats). SubnetEdge also dates activation Dec 24, 2025. add_stake_limit/remove_stake_limit take limit_price in RAO per alpha.

findings.claim: Other manipulation and failure patterns documented in 2025–2026: the SN28 memecoin feedback loop and its −98% collapse, owner-key compromise at ORO SN15, near-zero-volume tails, and bounded validator-take changes.
findings.detail:
- SN28, Mar 2025 (secondary, tzedonn Substack Mar 18, 2025): a taken-over subnet scored miners on how much SN28 alpha they held, creating a price → emission loop. It reached about #7 by market cap, then fell about 98% within hours after OTF ran custom validator code via root.
- ORO SN15, Jul 13, 2026 (secondary): owner wallet compromised by social engineering (attributed to Sapphire Sleet); 147k alpha drained and sold over about 10 hours (~$630K). The owner key had been kept in a software wallet.
- Validator take: delegate take is capped at 18% (InitialDefaultDelegateTake). Increases are rate-limited to once per 216,000 blocks (30 days; runtime SubtensorInitialTxDelegateTakeRateLimit=216000); decreases can happen anytime. Childkey take is per subnet with the same 30-day limit on increases. I found no documented take-change exploit against alpha stakers.
- Holder concentration (FalconX, May 2026): many subnets' top 20–50 holders control most supply, and only 9 subnets had more than 1,000 traders.
- Kraken listed SN8 for spot trading on Jul 16, 2026 (Kraken blog). That creates CEX/on-chain basis for large caps only.

verification.correction: The childkey take rate-limit value (TxChildKeyTakeRateLimit = INITIAL_CHILDKEY_TAKE_RATELIMIT) was not verified. The max childkey take is 18% (SubtensorInitialMaxChildKeyTake 11,796).
verification.evidence: MaxDelegateTake defaults to InitialDefaultDelegateTake = 11,796 (18%); on-chain null. increase_take enforces take <= MaxDelegateTake plus the TxDelegateTakeRateLimit; SubtensorInitialTxDelegateTakeRateLimit = 216000 (on-chain null). decrease_take has no rate check but stamps the last block. The Kraken blog says 'SN8 trading is live as of July 16, 2026'. ORO SN15 reporting (Jul 13, 2026, 147K alpha, ~$630K, attributed to Sapphire Sleet, owner key on a software wallet) is secondary but consistent. FalconX gives 9 subnets with more than 1,000 traders. SN28 is secondary and unchecked.

findings.claim: Root Reborn (v441, Jul 2026) stopped the old forced selling of root dividends (about 936 TAO/day of alpha sold into pools). Curated Beta (v450, Aug 2026) will route root dividends into validator baskets, a new and potentially concentrated buy flow for any micro cap a validator picks.
findings.detail:
v441 (block 8,922,321, 2026-07-24):
- Root dividends were previously 'sold into TAO the moment it arrived': 936 TAO/day, 78% of the ~1,196 TAO/day of emission entering pools then.
- At launch the 'null strategy' credits alpha with no swap, so net root flow is about 0.
- Snapshot: root stake 5,403,483 TAO (47.9% of 11.27M issued); base root yield 6.3%/yr; root dividend gate 1.32.

v450 Curated Beta:
- Validators set equal-weight vectors over at least 16 destinations, with RootWeightsCap = 1/16 (4096/65535).
- Pricing uses realisable (depth-bounded) quotes.
- Total β value about $4.5M, three weeks in.
- v461 (Sep 2026) basket trading launched gated off.

For micro caps: one validator's 1/16 slice bought into a 1,000–2,000-TAO pool is a meaningful, observable flow. Whether curation is live yet is unverified.

Currently the sum of moving prices is 1.185 (> 1, so root dividends are on).

verification.correction:
Three fixes:
1. The v441 page labels its snapshot 'finney block 8,922,321 · july 24, 2026', but block 8,922,321's on-chain timestamp is 2026-08-25 13:30 UTC. The page is internally inconsistent; do not use that block as a July 24 anchor.

Validator funds can swap_basket into micro caps, within limits: holding at most 10% of the destination pool's SubnetAlphaIn; daily turnover bucket 10% of NAV; concentration cap 1/16 of NAV; minimum trade 0.5 TAO; each leg bounded vs the slow EMA and a fast EMA (600-block half-life).
The v441 page also says root's 936 TAO/day was '26% of all new emission'.

findings.claim: Existing systematic alpha-trading tools and funds are mostly hobby repos, analysis dashboards or paid self-hosted bots without auditable track records. The only rigorous published factor evidence is Maymin (2026), plus my on-chain replication.
findings.detail:
Open source:
- 0xRozier/Bittensor-trading (French): hourly agent, z-scored factors. 24h and 7d log momentum, price vs on-chain EMA, net TAO flow / liquidity, emissions / market cap; weights 0.15/0.25/0.20/0.25/0.10 plus an APR term; 20–95% alpha allocation. Synthetic 180-day, 40-subnet backtest reports +22–34%, Sharpe 1.8–2.9, max drawdown 7–12%. Explicitly indicative only.
- buckZz7/dtao-trader: analysis tool (5-minute collector, SDK v11). Reads SubnetExcessTao as a 'chain-buy floor' and tracks emission kill switches. Claims emission harvesting about 1%/day is best; its '1% swap fee' figure is wrong.
- tududes/btt-subnet-dca: single-subnet EMA mean-reversion DCA with binary-search sizing to a slippage target.
- unconst gist (Jun 2025): rotates tiny amounts by (emission − price)/emission score.

Commercial (marketing claims):
- FlowSniper: $29/month, self-hosted, 16 on-chain signals, scans all subnets every 3 minutes. Modes: Sniper (momentum), Sentinel (5–15 subnets), Shadow (copy-trade). No published returns. Its 'Yield Illusion' claim (median realised 30-day return −7.2%, 73% of subnets losing) is undated and unverified.

api_details:
CHAIN DATA (no SDK needed; JSON-RPC over HTTPS)
- Current state: https://entrypoint-finney.opentensor.ai (state is pruned for old blocks; chain_getBlockHash still works for historical heights).
- Historical state:
  - https://bittensor-finney.api.onfinality.io/public was fast and showed no throttling in my tests (600 calls with 513 keys each in 155 s).
  - https://archive.chain.opentensor.ai allows a burst of about 13 historical calls, then returns error -32004 'Historical work rate limit exceeded' (budget historical_references). It refills over roughly 20 s.
- Storage key = '0x' + twox128(pallet) + twox128(item) + hasher(key).
  - SubtensorModule maps keyed by NetUid use the Identity hasher, so the key suffix is the u16 netuid little-endian, e.g. netuid 64 → '4000'.
  - Swap.FeeRate uses Twox64Concat: suffix = xxh64(le_u16, seed 0) as 8 bytes LE, followed by le_u16.
  - twox128(s) = xxh64(s, 0) as 8 bytes LE || xxh64(s, 1) as 8 bytes LE. Check: System.Number = 0x26aa394eea5630e07c48ae0c9558cef702a5c1b19ab7a04f536c519aca4983ac.
- Batch reads: state_queryStorageAt([keys...], blockHash) → result[0].changes = [[key, scaleHex|null]].
- Decoding:
  - u64 rao: int.from_bytes(bytes[0:8], 'little') / 1e9.
  - I96F32 / U96F32 (16 bytes): int / 2**32.
  - U64F64: int / 2**64.
  - bool: 0x01 / 0x00; null means the default (e.g. SubnetEmissionEnabled defaults to true, but registration explicitly writes false).
- Useful per-netuid items:
  - Pool and price: SubnetTAO (TAO reserve); SubnetAlphaIn (alpha reserve); SubnetAlphaOut (outstanding alpha); SubnetMovingPrice (I96F32 EMA price; the spot feed is capped at 1.0).
  - Registration and emission flags: NetworkRegisteredAt (block; a change means the netuid was recycled); SubnetEmissionEnabled; FirstEmissionBlockNumber.
  - Emission flows: SubnetTaoInEmission, SubnetExcessTao and SubnetAlphaInEmission (per block); SubnetAlphaOutEmission (per block; 1.0 when started); MinerBurned (U96F32); RootProp (U96F32); SubnetProtocolAlpha.
  - Global: EmissionGateBar (U64F64), EmissionBarRank (default 32), EmissionBarQuantile, EmissionGateExponent (default 3), NetworkImmunityPeriod (864,000), SubnetLimit (128), NetworkMinLockCost, NetworkLastLockCost, NetworkLockReductionInterval (115,200), NetworkRateLimit (14,400), TaoInRefundDeploymentBlock (8,334,450), Timestamp.Now (ms).
  - Swap pallet: Swap.FeeRate (u16; default 33 ≈ 0.05%), Swap.SwapBalancer (Perquintill quote weight; currently 0.5 everywhere).
- Runtime APIs (state_call): SwapRuntimeApi_current_alpha_price(netuid) → u64; SwapRuntimeApi_current_alpha_price_all() → Vec<{netuid, price}>; SwapRuntimeApi_sim_swap_tao_for_alpha(netuid, tao) and sim_swap_alpha_for_tao(netuid, alpha) → SimSwapResult{tao_amount, alpha_amount, tao_fee, alpha_fee, tao_slippage, alpha_slippage}.

FORMULAS
- Spot price: p = (w_tao·T)/(w_alpha·A); with weights 0.5/0.5, p = T/A.
- Buy alpha with Δ TAO: Δ' = Δ·(1 − FeeRate/65535); alpha_out = A·(1 − (T/(T+Δ'))^(w_tao/w_alpha)) → A·Δ'/(T+Δ'). Slippage vs spot = Δ'/(T+Δ'). Post-trade spot ×((T+Δ')/T)^2.
- Sell a alpha: tao_out = T·(1 − (A/(A+a'))^(w_alpha/w_tao)) → T·a'/(A+a'). Realisable value of a position worth V TAO at spot ≈ V·T/(T+V).
- Emission share (current):
  - s_i = MovingPrice_i / Σ MovingPrice;
  - s_i ← s_i·(1 − MinerBurned_i), then renormalise;
  - gate_i = 1/(1 + (θ/s_i)^h), with θ = the 32nd-largest share (recomputed every 360 blocks) and h = 3;
  - final_i ∝ s_i·gate_i, with disabled subnets' share redistributed;
  - TAO per block = BlockEmission(0.5 TAO post-halving) × final_i, split into tao_in (capped at RootProp × alpha emission × price) plus excess chain buys.
- EMA price: ema_alpha = base_alpha·blocks_since_start/(blocks_since_start + 201,600).
- Root proportion (docs): (root_tao·tao_weight)/(root_tao·tao_weight + alpha_issuance); TaoWeight is 0.18 on-chain.
- Prune candidate = argmin SubnetMovingPrice over added non-root netuids with current_block ≥ NetworkRegisteredAt + NetworkImmunityPeriod; ties go to the earliest registration.
- Dereg payout: holder_i gets SubnetTAO·alpha_i/(Σ holder alpha + protocol alpha [+ SubnetAlphaIn if reg_at > 8,334,450]), credited to coldkey free balance.
- Legacy-taoflow (dead code): z_i = max(EMA_flow_i − L, 0), L = max{TaoFlowCutoff, min(min S, 0)}; share = z^p/Σz^p; flow EMA half-life 216,000 blocks.
- Maymin size-premium mechanism: return ≈ 2Δτ/τ for emission Δτ staked into a pool with τ TAO.

TAOSTATS API (needs an Authorization header with an API key; free key from taostats.io/pro/api-keys)
- GET /api/dtao/pool/history/v1?netuid=&frequency=by_block|by_hour|by_day&block_start=&block_end=&timestamp_start=&timestamp_end=&page=&limit<=200&order=
  - Required fields: price, market_cap, liquidity, total_tao, total_alpha, alpha_in_pool, alpha_staked, root_prop, rank, startup_mode.
  - Optional (nullable) fields: fee_rate, protocol_provided_tao/alpha, user_provided_tao/alpha.
- GET /api/dtao/tao_flow/v1?netuid=&block_start=&block_end=&timestamp_start=&timestamp_end= → {netuid, tao_flow}.
- Also: /api/subnet/get-pool-latest, /api/delegation/get-slippage, /api/delegation/get-trade.

EXECUTION (SDK v11; from docs, not tested here)
- Example: client.submit_shielded(bt.AddStakeLimit(hotkey_ss58=..., netuid=..., amount_tao=..., limit_price_rao=int(spot_price_rao*1.01), allow_partial=False), wallet). RemoveStakeLimit mirrors it with floor = spot × (1 − tol).
- MEV Shield works only for coldkey-signed extrinsics.
- Delegate take is capped at 18%; increases are rate-limited to 216,000 blocks.
- Swap fee 0.05% per side goes to the block author.
api_corrections:
TAOSTATS
- `/api/subnet/get-pool-latest`, `/api/delegation/get-slippage` and `/api/delegation/get-trade` do not exist: all three return HTTP 404. Live equivalents (each returns 401 without a key, so the route exists):
  - `/api/dtao/pool/latest/v1`
  - `/api/dtao/slippage/v1`
  - `/api/dtao/trade/v1`
  - `/api/delegation/v1`
  - `/api/dtao/subnet_emission/v1`
- `/api/dtao/pool/history/v1` and `/api/dtao/tao_flow/v1` exist (401 without a key). Their field lists were not verified.

RPC
- entrypoint-finney.opentensor.ai is rate-limited: `{"error":"Too many requests from this source.","policy":"http_60s","retry_after_seconds":60}` after a burst of ~128 batched calls.
- The OnFinality public endpoint returns -32029 'Too Many Requests, Please apply an OnFinality API key' at ~8 concurrent requests. It is fine sequentially.

STORAGE / FORMULAS
- Do not read `SubtensorModule.BlockEmission`. It still stores 1e9 rao (1 TAO). The real emission is DefaultBlockEmission × 2^-floor(log2(1/(1 - issuance/21e15))) = 0.5 TAO at TotalIssuance 11.60M (block_emission.rs).
- EMA price formula: alpha_t = SubnetMovingAlpha × b/(b + EMAPriceHalvingBlocks[netuid]).
  - SubnetMovingAlpha on-chain is 0.0003 (I96F32 raw 1,288,490). The code default is 0.000003.
  - EMAPriceHalvingBlocks defaults to 201,600; it is null for all netuids.
  - b = blocks since FirstEmissionBlockNumber - 1. Spot is clamped at 1.0.
- Lock cost: max(NetworkMinLockCost, 2·NetworkLastLockCost − NetworkLastLockCost·(now − last_lock_block)/(NetworkLockReductionInterval × block_emission/1e9)).
  - last_lock_block is in LastRateLimitedBlock[RateLimitKey::NetworkLastRegistered].
  - The effective interval is 57,600 blocks.
  - Query it with state_call `SubnetRegistrationRuntimeApi_get_network_registration_cost`: 965.70 TAO on 2026-10-08.
- Alpha emission per subnet = get_block_emission_for_issuance(SubnetAlphaIn + SubnetAlphaOut + protocol reservoir). It is not a constant 1.0.
- `SwapBalancer` is a `Balancer{quote: Perquintill}` (TAO weight) stored as 8-byte u64 parts/1e18. Live values are 0.49999974–0.5.
- The 1000× input cap applies to SubnetTAO for buys and to SubnetAlphaIn for sells. Both return InsufficientLiquidity in the subtensor pallet; the swap pallet uses SwapInputTooLarge.
- Dereg payout: SubnetProtocolAlpha is a subset of SubnetAlphaOut (chain-buy alpha is added to AlphaOut), so do not add both when approximating.
- Owner-refund eligibility uses NetworkRegistrationStartBlock = 6,573,966, not TaoInRefundDeploymentBlock.

SDK
- opentensor/bittensor is archived (now RaoFoundation/bittensor; last tag v10.5.0, 2026-06-25). opentensor/subtensor redirects to RaoFoundation/subtensor.
- SDK v11 lives in that monorepo at `sdk/python/bittensor`. PyPI bittensor is at 11.3.0 (2026-10-07), Python >=3.10,<3.15.
- The client is async (`async with bt.Subtensor() as client`; `bt.SyncClient` also exists). `submit_shielded` must be awaited: `await client.submit_shielded(intent, wallet, *, policy=None, proxy_for=None, proxy_type=None, period=MEV_SHIELD_ERA_PERIOD, wait_for_inclusion=True, wait_for_finalization=False, ...)`.
- `bt.AddStakeLimit` fields are `hotkey_ss58`, `netuid`, `amount_tao`, `limit_price_rao`, `allow_partial=False`. These are correct.
- `client.execute()` does not shield by default; only btcli defaults to MEV shield for staking intents.
- The chain extrinsic is `add_stake_limit(hotkey, netuid, amount_staked, limit_price, allow_partial)`, with limit_price in RAO per alpha.
missed_critical_facts: The emission and prune EMA reacts within hours, not weeks. On-chain SubnetMovingAlpha is 0.0003, 100x the code default of 0.000003 ('30 days to reach 50%'). For a mature subnet the half-life is ~ln2/0.0003 ≈ 2,310 blocks ≈ 7.7 h (alpha_t = 0.0003·b/(b+201,600)). Pushing spot for under a day therefore moves emission share and prune rank. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RaoFoundation/subtensor/main/pallets/subtensor/src/staking/stake_utils.rs plus the SubtensorModule.SubnetMovingAlpha read via https://entrypoint-finney.opentensor.ai.

SubtensorModule.BlockEmission storage is stale at 1 TAO. The actual block emission is computed from issuance and is 0.5 TAO, confirmed by per-block injections summing to 0.500000. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RaoFoundation/subtensor/main/pallets/subtensor/src/coinbase/block_emission.rs

Subnet registration cost decays over 57,600 blocks, not 115,200, because get_lock_reduction_interval scales by block emission. The cost on 2026-10-08 was 965.70 TAO, from the runtime API SubnetRegistrationRuntimeApi_get_network_registration_cost. This sets how often pruning can happen. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RaoFoundation/subtensor/main/pallets/subtensor/src/coinbase/root.rs

Pruning happens only when a new subnet registers, at most once per 14,400 blocks network-wide. At capacity the new registration is queued behind a multi-block DissolveCleanupQueue/NetworkRegistrationQueue. The netuid is not instantly recycled, and the payout phases run over several blocks. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RaoFoundation/subtensor/main/pallets/subtensor/src/subnets/subnet.rs and .../subnets/dissolution.rs

Subnets that never call start_call have EMA 0, so they become the very next prune targets once immune: SN86 in ~316,679 blocks (~2026-11-21), then SN59 and SN82. SN86 has gone 76 days without starting, so start can be delayed indefinitely. Source: on-chain FirstEmissionBlockNumber/SubnetMovingPrice/NetworkRegisteredAt via https://entrypoint-finney.opentensor.ai and get_network_to_prune in https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RaoFoundation/subtensor/main/pallets/subtensor/src/coinbase/root.rs

Validator basket trading is enabled on-chain (BasketTradingEnabled=true, set by migrate_enable_basket_trading after v461 launched gated off). It is a new discretionary flow into and out of micro caps. Caps:
- A holding may not exceed 10% of the destination pool's alpha reserve.
- Turnover is limited to 10% of NAV per day.
- One holding may not exceed 1/16 of NAV.
- Minimum trade is 0.5 TAO.
- Price bounds use a fast EMA with a 600-block half-life.
Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RaoFoundation/subtensor/main/pallets/subtensor/src/migrations/migrate_enable_basket_trading.rs and lib.rs

Owner-cut auto-lock is off by default (OwnerCutAutoLockEnabled=false) and enabled on only 13 subnets (17, 31, 34, 51, 53, 64, 73, 87, 90, 96, 106, 109, 122). Conviction locks unlock with tau = 934,866 blocks, about 50% after ~90 days. Owner dumping risk is therefore not mitigated on ~115 subnets. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RaoFoundation/subtensor/main/pallets/subtensor/src/lib.rs plus on-chain reads

Per-subnet alpha emission halves when SubnetAlphaIn + SubnetAlphaOut + protocol reservoir reaches 10.5M (primary code, get_subnet_terms). The leaders are at ~6.4M (SN4, SN64, SN12), so the first per-subnet halvings are around 2028. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RaoFoundation/subtensor/main/pallets/subtensor/src/coinbase/run_coinbase.rs

Emission eligibility also requires network registration to be allowed. get_subnets_to_emit_to filters on FirstEmissionBlockNumber set, SubtokenEnabled, and get_network_registration_allowed. A subnet that disables registration drops out of emission sharing entirely, and its EMA stops updating. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RaoFoundation/subtensor/main/pallets/subtensor/src/coinbase/subnet_emissions.rs and coinbase/block_step.rs

The code moved. opentensor/subtensor is now RaoFoundation/subtensor. opentensor/bittensor is archived (last tag v10.5.0, Jun 25, 2026), and SDK v11 lives at sdk/python in the subtensor monorepo (PyPI bittensor 11.3.0, released 2026-10-07). Source: https://api.github.com/repositories/608683796 and https://pypi.org/pypi/bittensor/json

The public RPCs throttle. entrypoint-finney returns 'Too many requests from this source' (policy http_60s, retry_after 60s), and the OnFinality public endpoint returns -32029 under concurrency. A production algo needs its own node or a keyed provider. Source: observed responses from https://entrypoint-finney.opentensor.ai and https://bittensor-finney.api.onfinality.io/public

The gate went live at block ~8,713,815 (2026-07-27 14:20 UTC), the first block with EmissionGateBar non-zero. The v441 page's snapshot block 8,922,321 is actually dated 2026-08-25, not July 24. Source: archive reads via https://archive.chain.opentensor.ai and https://www.bittensor.com/releases/v441-upgrade
open_questions: SubnetProtocolAlpha semantics: whether it is already included in SubnetAlphaOut, and so how exact my 0.45–1.0× (legacy) and 0.3–0.5× (new) deregistration recovery ratios are. Checking would need the full body of destroy_alpha_in_out_stakes_get_total_alpha_value and transfer_tao_from_subnet, or a replay of an actual dissolution block such as SN116 on 2026-10-05.

Whether gate-era momentum (WML7 +0.45%/day, t 2.4) and the reversed size premium (−0.56%/day) persist. The post-June-2026 sample is only 73–109 days. Both are gross of slippage and fees, and capacity in sub-3,000-TAO pools is tiny.
Whether root has enabled Curated Beta weight-setting (v450) and basket trading (v461) on mainnet, and how much root-dividend flow is reaching small subnets now.

Owner-cut auto-lock default under Conviction: tao.media says owner emissions are auto-locked from 2026-05-13, but another source says owner_cut_auto_lock_enabled is off by default, and v439 added controls. This needs an on-chain storage check per subnet.

Doc/chain conflicts to resolve before hard-coding constants. NetworkImmunityPeriod is 864,000 on-chain vs 1,296,000 in the docs; NetworkMinLockCost is 1 TAO on-chain vs 1,000 TAO in the docs; NetworkRateLimit is 14,400 blocks on-chain vs 7,200 in the docs and 4 days on taostats; StartCallDelay is 0 vs older 7-day behaviour; the gate bar is around 'rank 32' in the text vs 'RANK 33' in the v440 chart.
The planned subnet-cap expansion to 256 and the 'Null Consensus' release. Either would change slot scarcity, deregistration cadence (currently about weekly) and gate dynamics.

There is no quantitative on-chain study of first-block sniping on new subnets or of sandwich losses before and after MEV Shield. My cohort-C data (since Apr 2026) shows only a +9% median 14-day max run-up, but sniping within a block is not visible at daily resolution.

Volume and turnover for micro caps. CoinGecko's 24h volumes (e.g. under $1K for several subnets) may not capture all on-chain swap volume; taostats subnet volume or summed swap events would be needed.
My launch and deregistration date resolution is daily (7,200-block sampling). Exact event blocks and timestamps would need event scans (NetworkAdded/NetworkRemoved).
USD beta for Feb–Oct 2025 could not be computed, because the free CoinGecko API limits history to 365 days; the TAO-denominated statistics for that period are still valid.

summary:
As of 2026-10-08 the protocol is moving fast, and protocol and operational risk matter more than market risk for a micro-cap alpha bot. Code now lives under the GitHub org RaoFoundation (opentensor/* redirects there). Mainnet is on runtime spec 475 (Oct 7, 2026), and 476 is proposed. From Sep 17 to Oct 7, 2026 there were roughly 7 live runtime upgrades, several of them hotfixes that changed staking bookkeeping, fees or nonce handling. Upgrades need a 2-of-2 multisig (CI plus the triumvirate), and no public notice period was found. The Python SDK was rewritten as bittensor 11.x (11.0.0 on 2026-07-17; latest 11.3.0 on 2026-10-07). It now uses intents (AddStakeLimit, RemoveStakeLimit and others), turns MEV-shield on by default for stake trades, and adds a 5% default slippage bound. The old opentensor/bittensor repo was archived on 2026-07-10, and the SDK now publishes from RaoFoundation/subtensor through PyPI Trusted Publishing. The subnet emission rule has changed about 5 times in 11 months, with little or no warning: Taoflow (Nov 2025), Net Tao Flow (May 2026), back to price EMA (Jun 23, 2026), the emission gate (spec 440, Jul 27, 2026), and the miner-burn scaling flip-flop (Aug 2026). The emission gate pushes emission for tail subnets toward zero. In the published snapshot, below-bar subnets held about 38% of demand but earned about 10% of emission. Separately, root can switch off TAO emission for a subnet (57 of 128 on Jun 22, 2026, reviewed every Monday). When that happens, TAO and alpha injection into the pool stop but alpha_out keeps diluting holders. Micro-caps are therefore structurally the subnets most likely to be gated, switched off or deregistered.

Exit mechanics: there is no unbonding, and the current code has no active per-block staking rate limit. The StakingRateLimitExceeded error is declared but unused. Exits are bounded by pool depth (selling a position worth V TAO at spot into a TAO reserve T loses about V/(T+V)). They can also be blocked by conviction locks, miner collateral, AmountTooLow on partial remainders below 0.002 TAO, InsufficientLiquidity, or a root-forced SafeMode of 7,200 blocks or more. July 2024 lasted 10 days. On deregistration, holders get TAO pro rata from the subnet's TAO pot. The denominator includes protocol-owned alpha, and for subnets registered after block 8,334,450 it also includes the pool alpha reserve. The protocol's share is recycled. As a result the liquidation price per alpha is usually far below spot, so a bot should exit dereg candidates before pruning rather than hold through it.

Execution and key risks: sandwiching is mitigated, not eliminated, by limit-price extrinsics and the MEV Shield. The shield uses ML-KEM-768 + XChaCha20-Poly1305 and was activated around 2025-12-24 according to a secondary source. Shielded transactions are coldkey-only with an 8-block era, and the PoA block author still decrypts them. Keys have been the main loss vector: the PyPI bittensor 6.12.2 compromise (about 32k TAO, about $8M, chain in safe mode July 2-12, 2024); the Aug 6, 2025 typosquat packages that hijacked stake_extrinsic into transfer_all; and July 2026 social-engineering drains of subnet-owner wallets (ORO SN15: 147k alpha dumped over about 10h). The recommended setup is a cold or offline coldkey plus a narrowly scoped Staking proxy for the bot, with pinned and hash-verified dependencies. A Staking proxy can still move or swap stake, so a leaked bot key can be used to force value-destroying trades into thin pools. Owner and concentration risk is large: an 18% owner cut, top-20 holders driving volume in about a third of subnets, only 4 subnets with more than $1M of 2% depth (May 2026), and Covenant's April 2026 exit (subnet tokens down 40-50% almost immediately). This is research, not financial or tax advice.

findings.claim: Subnet deregistration pays alpha holders TAO pro rata from the subnet TAO pot. The denominator includes protocol-owned alpha, and for newer subnets also the pool alpha reserve, so the liquidation price per alpha is typically far below spot. Exiting before pruning beats holding through it.
findings.detail: Payout: holder_TAO = holder_alpha_value × liq_price. For subnets registered at or before block 8,334,450 (TaoInRefundDeploymentBlock): liq_price = SubnetTAO / (α_staked + SubnetProtocolAlpha). For subnets registered after 8,334,450: liq_price = SubnetTAO / (α_staked + SubnetProtocolAlpha + SubnetAlphaIn). α_staked is the sum of every staker's share-pool value, not SubnetAlphaOut. Since runtime 415 (subtensor v3.4.2-415) the protocol's share (protocol alpha, plus alpha_in for new subnets) is recycled and not paid to stakers. Code: pallets/subtensor/src/staking/remove_stake.rs destroy_alpha_in_out_stakes{_get_total_alpha_value,_settle_stakes,_clean_alpha,_clear_locks,_clear_decaying_locks}, driven from subnets/dissolution.rs. The cleanup is cursor-based across blocks: the pot is drained at block x and coldkey free balances are credited over blocks x..y. Rounding remainders go to the largest remainders. Lock and conviction records are deleted. A legacy-owner refund = max(0, lock_cost − owner emissions in TAO) applies only to subnets registered before NetworkRegistrationStartBlock 6,573,966. Spec 468 (2026-09-21) changed dissolution again ('restores only the deducted amount in dissolution stake'). Selection (coinbase/root.rs get_network_to_prune): among added, non-root subnets past immunity (current_block ≥ NetworkRegisteredAt + NetworkImmunityPeriod), the lowest get_moving_alpha_price (EMA) is pruned; ties go to the earliest registration. Pruning is triggered when a new subnet registers at the SubnetLimit cap (DefaultSubnetLimit = 128). Deregistration returned on 2025-09-17 (PR #2066) with immunity of 4 months = 864,000 blocks; the runtime Initial constant is 1,296,000, so read the live storage. Root can also dissolve any subnet with root_dissolve_network(origin, netuid) (dispatches.rs L2064). Intuition: for new subnets, liq_price equals what every staker would get if all sold at once, which is much worse than an individual early exit at spot.

verification.correction: The core mechanics are confirmed by the code. Three corrections apply. (a) PR #2066 is titled "mainnet deploy 9/25/2025" and was merged 2025-09-25, not 2025-09-17. It brought dereg back with a 4-month immunity and raised NetworkRateLimit from 2 to 4 days. Live NetworkRateLimit is now 14,400 blocks (about 2 days), not 7,200 and not 4 days. (b) The runtime-415 link is inferred from timing, not stated in the release notes. TaoInRefundDeploymentBlock is set by a migration to the upgrade block. Live it is 8,334,450, which is 2026-06-04 16:49 UTC, the day after the v3.4.2-415 release (2026-06-03). Those release notes only mention 'Fix chain buys accounting' (#2706). (c) 'Protocol share is recycled' is not universal. For legacy subnets (NetworkRegisteredAt < NetworkRegistrationStartBlock = 6,573,966) the owner refund is max(0, lock_cost − owner_emission_tao), plus any pot leftover, capped at subnet-account balance − protocol_tao_share. Mechanics: do_dissolve_network removes NetworksAdded immediately, subtracts SubnetTAO from TotalStake and queues the netuid in DissolveCleanupQueue. Payout then runs in on_idle across blocks: SubnetBasketHoldingsToRoot → GetTotalAlphaValue → SettleStakes (transfer_tao_from_subnet per coldkey) → clean alpha/hotkey totals/locks/decaying locks → AlphaInOutStakes, which recycles the remainder and removes SubnetTAO. Registration at the cap can also be queued (NetworkRegistrationQueued) when cleanup is pending.

findings.claim: The emission gate (spec 440, live 2026-07-27) pushes emission for tail and micro-cap subnets toward zero, so most micro-caps now get little or no TAO injection.
findings.detail: Demand share s_i = movingPrice_i·(1−minerBurned_i) / Σ_j movingPrice_j·(1−minerBurned_j). Gate g(s) = s^h/(s^h+θ^h) = 1/(1+(θ/s)^h), with h = 3 by default (sudo-settable 1..8). Emission e_i = s_i·g(s_i)/Σ s_j·g(s_j). Subnets with SubnetEmissionEnabled=false are then zeroed and renormalized. θ is recomputed every 360 blocks. Taostats defines θ as the share at which the sorted cumulative share reaches q = 0.61 (snapshot θ = 1.339% at rank 18, block 8,714,269). The bittensor.com emissions doc instead says θ = the 32nd-highest positive adjusted share. These conflict; verify in subnet_emissions.rs. Snapshot effect: below-bar subnets held about 38% of demand but earned about 10% of emission. At s = θ the gate is 0.5; well below θ it is about 0. Source PR #2800. No announcement lead time is documented. Example: Quasar SN24 emissions fell about 86% in the v440 reshuffle (secondary). Moving price EMA: ema_alpha = base_alpha × blocks_since_start/(blocks_since_start + 201,600), and the spot price fed into the EMA is capped at 1.0, so new subnets adapt very slowly.

verification.correction: The gate formula, h=3 (root-settable 1..8), the 360-block recompute, zeroing of disabled subnets with renormalization, and the EMA formula are all correct. The θ conflict is settled by current code. Since release 441 (Root Reborn, #2968, 2026-08-03) the bar runs in RANK mode: EmissionBarRank default N=32, so θ is the 32nd-largest positive share. q-mass mode applies only if root sets the rank to 0. Live: EmissionBarRank is unset (default 32), EmissionBarQuantile is stored as 0.75 (dormant), EmissionGateExponent is unset (3), and EmissionGateBar ≈ 0.008262 (θ ≈ 0.83%). The taostats q=0.61 / rank-18 snapshot describes the spec-440 state on 2026-07-27, now superseded. bittensor.com's '32nd-highest' is current. PR #2800 did not introduce the gate. #2800 is 'Enforce conviction' (merged 2026-06-30), which also removed root_prop from the emission calculation. The gate shipped in commit 791e999 'release v440: emission gate, subnet limit 256, docs preview' (2026-07-27). Taostats wrongly cites #2800 too. Also, the gate is computed BEFORE disabled subnets are zeroed, so emission-disabled subnets still occupy ranks for θ. EMA detail: base alpha = SubnetMovingAlpha, live 0.0003 per block (code default 0.000003). The halving term is per-netuid EMAPriceHalvingBlocks (default 201,600). The input spot price is capped at 1.0. The EMA updates only for subnets in the emit set (start_call done, SubtokenEnabled, registration allowed).
verification.evidence: subnet_emissions.rs main and v475 tag. get_shares = price-EMA shares → scale_price_shares_by_miner_burn → maybe_update_emission_gate_bar (EMISSION_BAR_UPDATE_INTERVAL=360; rank mode if EmissionBarRank>0, else q-mass) → apply_emission_gate (gate = 1/(1+(θ/s)^h), renormalize, restore ungated if all zero). get_subnet_block_emissions zeroes disabled subnets and renormalizes. lib.rs: DefaultEmissionBarRank=32 (comment: 'Near the pre-upgrade q=0.75 crossing (~rank 28)… rank mode then tracks N=32'), DefaultEmissionBarQuantile=0.61, DefaultEmissionGateExponent=3. admin-utils sudo_set_emission_gate_exponent: ensure 1 ≤ h ≤ 8. migrate_reset_emission_gate_bar was added in #2968, dated 2026-08-03. stake_utils.rs update_moving_price: alpha = SubnetMovingAlpha * b/(b+EMAPriceHalvingBlocks), with current_alpha_price.min(1.0). Live RPC values as stated. PR #2800 page title is 'Enforce conviction'.

findings.claim: Emission rules change often and with little or no warning: about 5 subnet-emission formula regimes from Feb 2025 to Aug 2026. A bot must not hard-code an emission model.
findings.detail: Timeline: (1) dTAO launch Feb 2025, first dTAO block 4,920,351; shares by EMA price. (2) Taoflow Nov 2025, 100% of emission by Dec 2025: share ∝ EMA of net staking flow, 30-day half-life (per-block keep 0.99997), negative flows floored at 0. (3) Net Tao Flow May 2026: EMA(flow) − EMA(protocol cost). (4) Price-based shares, live 2026-06-23 (PRs #2779/#2781), share ∝ price EMA × (1 − miner_burned); PR #2800 removed root_proportion weighting (as of 2026-06-30). (5) Emission gate, spec 440, 2026-07-27. (6) Runtime 445 (2026-08-12) removed miner-burn scaling (#3058) and restored it (#3071) within the same release. Also the first halving in Dec 2025 (1 → 0.5 TAO/block, about 3,600 TAO/day). Halvings are triggered by total-issuance thresholds (10.5M, 15.75M, ...), and recycling delays them. Secondary sources (e.g. Backpack, updated 2026-07-09) still describe Taoflow as current, so third-party data can be stale.

findings.claim: Root can switch off TAO emission for a subnet (SubnetEmissionEnabled = false). Since 2026-06-22 OTF does this weekly (Mondays) for subnets without active miner distribution or code. Holders then face alpha dilution with no TAO injection.
findings.detail: On 2026-06-22 emissions stopped for 57 of 128 subnets, announced by Const on Discord. Criteria: no miner distribution (a 'non active mechanism') or no code. Cadence: weekly on Mondays. Reinstatement is case by case. No lead time was given and the effect was immediate (tao.media). Mechanics: an emission-disabled subnet gets no TAO-side share (redistributed to enabled subnets), and its tao_in and alpha_in injections stop, but alpha_out keeps accruing. That means sell-side dilution with no new TAO deepening the pool. The hyperparameter subnet_emission_enabled is root-only. The bot should poll this flag every block or epoch and treat a flip to false as an exit signal.

verification.correction: The 2026-06-22 event is confirmed: 57 subnet IDs listed, announced by Const on Discord, criteria 'non active mechanism' or no code, weekly on Mondays, reinstatement case by case, no notice mentioned. The mechanics are confirmed by code. However, the live state on 2026-10-08 (block ~9,240,418) is that only 6 of 128 subnets have SubnetEmissionEnabled=false: netuids 29, 35, 36, 82, 108, 116. Most of the June list was reinstated or replaced. Whether the weekly cadence continues is unverified. Additional mechanics: a disabled subnet also loses its per-block 'chain buys' (excess-TAO protocol purchases of alpha). Its moving price keeps updating. It still counts in the emission-gate rank. The flip emits AdminUtils event SubnetEmissionEnabledSet{netuid, enabled}, which is better to subscribe to than polling.

Live state_queryStorageAt over SubnetEmissionEnabled[1..128]: 122 true, 6 false.

findings.claim: There is no unbonding and no active per-block stake or unstake rate limit for non-root subnets in current code. A position can still be trapped by locks, collateral, minimums, liquidity checks or a root-forced SafeMode.
findings.detail: validate_remove_stake (staking/stake_utils.rs L1578) checks: SubnetNotExists; AmountTooLow if the amount is 0; NotEnoughStakeToWithdraw; InsufficientLiquidity if sim_swap fails; AmountTooLow if a partial unstake pays out below DefaultMinStake (full exits are exempt); SlippageTooHigh (limit variants with allow_partial=false); HotKeyAccountNotExists; ensure_available_to_unstake (available = total − locked − collateral, else StakeUnavailable); ensure_hotkey_covers_collateral; and for root only, ensure_root_stake_unlocked (RootStakeUnlockInterval, default 0 = disabled). ensure_subtoken_enabled is commented out for remove_stake, so you can exit a not-started subnet, but add_stake requires SubtokenEnabled. TransferToggle (owner-settable 'transfers_enabled', default true) only gates transfer_stake/move/swap paths (TransferDisallowed), not remove_stake. StakingRateLimitExceeded is declared in macros/errors.rs L95 but has no other references, and guards/check_rate_limits.rs rate-limits only weight commits/sets and register_network. Runtime 473 (2026-10-05) added a rate limit on 'delegated alpha hotkey moves'. SafeMode pallet (index 20): permissionless entry disabled (EnterDuration = 0); root ForceEnter lasts RootEnterDuration = 5×60×24 = 7,200 blocks (24h) and can be extended. The July 2024 safe mode ran July 2–12. DefaultMinStake = SubtensorInitialMinStake = 2,000,000 rao (0.002 TAO). DefaultMinTransfer = 100,000 rao.

findings.claim: Exit liquidity in a micro-cap pool is bounded by the TAO reserve, not by time. Immediate exit loss vs spot ≈ V/(T+V), so keep positions to a small percentage of the pool's TAO reserve.
findings.detail: Pools are protocol-owned weighted (balancer) pools with reserves SubnetTAO (T) and SubnetAlphaIn (A), weights near 0.5/0.5. Spot p = (w1·T)/(w2·A) ≈ T/A. Invariant L = x^w1·y^w2. There are no external LPs, and user_liquidity_enabled is off by default (SDK v11 removed the liquidity features). Swap fee FeeRate default 33/65535 ≈ 0.05%, taken from the input and paid to the block author. With equal weights: selling ΔA alpha gives TAO_out = T·ΔA/(A+ΔA). For a position of spot value V = ΔA·T/A, the shortfall vs spot = V/(T+V). Max size for exit slippage s: V_max = T·s/(1−s), so 1% → 1.01% of T, 2% → 2.04%, 5% → 5.26%, 10% → 11.1%. Buying ΔT costs ΔT/(T+ΔT) in alpha terms. A round trip costs roughly 2s plus fees. Example: T = 2,000 TAO with a 100 TAO position gives about a 4.8% exit loss if no one else trades. Splitting into tranches only helps if buyers or injections refill the pool between tranches. For gated or emission-disabled subnets tao_in ≈ 0, so the pool does not deepen. Trades that would drain a reserve below a minimum return InsufficientLiquidity. Market context, May 2026: only 4 subnets had AMM 2% depth above $1M.

verification.correction: The pool is a balancer pool, but the weights are not fixed at 0.5. Per-subnet weights live in Swap.SwapBalancer and are re-solved on every protocol injection. Code bound: each weight ≥ MIN_WEIGHT 0.01; the comment says [0.1, 0.9]. Liquidity that cannot be injected sits in BalancerTaoReservoir/BalancerAlphaReservoir. Docs say the weights stay near 0.5 in practice. The general exit formula, with w1 = alpha (base) weight and w2 = TAO (quote) weight, is TAO_out = T·(1 − (A/(A+ΔA))^(w1/w2)) and spot p = w1·T/(w2·A). V/(T+V) is exact only for w1 = w2, so read SwapBalancer live. FeeRate default 33/65535 is per-subnet and root-settable up to SwapMaxFeeRate 10,000/65,535 (15.26%). The fee comes off the input and goes 100% to the block author: TAO when staking; alpha when unstaking, swapped to TAO or burned. User liquidity is not just off by default: all LP extrinsics (add/remove/modify_liquidity, toggle_user_liquidity, disable_lp) now return Deprecated. Swaps that would leave a reserve below MinimumReserve = 1,000,000 rao fail with ReservesTooLow, which surfaces as InsufficientLiquidity. The FalconX figure is confirmed ('only 4 subnets have AMM 2% depth of $1M+', as of 2026-05-13, CoinGecko-sourced, secondary). Also, besides tao_in injection, emitting subnets receive per-block protocol 'chain buys' of alpha from excess TAO. Those vanish when a subnet is gated or disabled.
verification.evidence: pallets/swap/src/pallet/balancer.rs header formulas: Price p = (w1*y)/(w2*x); sell ∆y = y*((x/(x+∆x))^(w1/w2) − 1); weights adjusted on added liquidity; MIN_WEIGHT = ACCURACY/100. mod.rs: DefaultFeeRate 33, SwapBalancer, reservoirs, deprecated LP calls. swap_step.rs: '100% of swap fees to block builder'. stake_utils.rs settle_alpha_fee_to_author/settle_tao_fee_to_author. runtime lib.rs: SwapMaxFeeRate 10000, SwapMinimumReserve 1_000_000. run_coinbase.rs inject_and_maybe_swap. Staking-pools doc says the weights 'stay near 0.5 in practice'.

findings.claim: The primary sandwich and slippage mitigation is the chain-enforced limit price (add_stake_limit / remove_stake_limit / swap_stake_limit). Defaults differ by SDK version, and v10 defaults to no protection.
findings.detail: Chain: the chain fills up to the point where the pool price reaches limit_price. allow_partial=true stops at the limit; false rejects the whole order with SlippageTooHigh. SDK v10: add_stake(..., safe_staking=False, allow_partial_stake=False, rate_tolerance=0.005), so protection is opt-in. SDK v11 (bittensor 11.x): bt.AddStakeLimit(hotkey_ss58, netuid, amount_tao, limit_price_rao, allow_partial) and bt.RemoveStakeLimit(...). Plain AddStake, RemoveStake, SwapStake, MoveStake and MoveSwapStake get a default 5% price bound (opt out with slippage_protection=False / --no-slippage-protection). The 5% default is stated in the migration doc; I could not find it in the indexed Rust code because it is SDK-side. Ceiling = spot × (1 + tol); floor = spot × (1 − tol). The docs example uses spot × 1.02 with allow_partial=False. Talisman applies its own slippage cap and recommends splitting orders. Basket trades are capped at 2% slippage per leg.

verification.evidence: Chain: add_stake_limit(hotkey, netuid, amount_staked, limit_price, allow_partial). With allow_partial=false, validate_* ensures amount ≤ max_amount, else SlippageTooHigh. SDK v10.5.0 subtensor.py add_stake(wallet, netuid, hotkey_ss58, amount, safe_staking=False, allow_partial_stake=False, rate_tolerance=0.005, *, mev_protection=DEFAULT_MEV_PROTECTION, ...). SDK v11 source sdk/python/bittensor/intents/staking.py: DEFAULT_RATE_TOLERANCE = 0.05; AddStake/RemoveStake have slippage_protection=True by default and compose add_stake_limit with limit_price=int(price*(1+rate_tolerance)), allow_partial=False. Cross-subnet MoveStake/SwapStake use the *_limit call, fill-or-kill. AddStakeLimit fields: hotkey_ss58, netuid, amount_tao, limit_price_rao, allow_partial=False. The staking guide example uses spot['price_rao']*1.02 with allow_partial=False. Talisman applies an automatic slippage cap and says 'Split large stakes or unstakes'. The Root Reborn guide says each AMM leg 'must fill within 2% of the subnet's moving and spot price'.

findings.claim: MEV Shield (encrypted mempool) hides stake trades until inclusion but has limits: coldkey-signed only, an 8-block era, a two-nonce scheme, decryption by the PoA block author, and metadata leakage.
findings.detail: Mechanism: the signed inner extrinsic is encrypted to the rotating ML-KEM-768 key (mev-shield-next-key) with XChaCha20-Poly1305 and carried in MevShield.submit_encrypted; the block author decrypts at block-build time. Payload max 8,192 bytes. Runtime config pallet_shield: ShieldSlotMs = SLOT_DURATION, ShieldAnnounceAtMs = 7,000, ShieldGraceMs = 2,000, ShieldDecryptWindowMs = 3,000. Activated on mainnet around 2025-12-24 (secondary: Subnet Edge). Defaults: SDK v10 mev_protection=False unless BT_MEV_PROTECTION is in {1,true,yes,on}; wait_for_revealed_execution=True, blocks_for_revealed_execution=5. SDK v11 renames it mev_shield, on by default for stake-trading intents (CLI --mev-shield/--no-mev-shield; client.submit_shielded(intent, wallet)). Constraints: hotkey-signed extrinsics fail; wrapper and inner extrinsic both use an 8-block era (the chain rejects longer); outer wrapper nonce N, inner N+1 (SDK v10.3.2 fixed a shield nonce-increment bug); outcomes are EncryptedSubmitted then DecryptedExecuted or DecryptedRejected; the wrapper pays a fee. Residual risks: (a) the signer and timing are visible, so with a single alpha position bots can infer an incoming unstake (Talisman); (b) block production is Proof-of-Authority, so the authority decrypting your trade is trusted; (c) swaps well under about 1 TAO gain nothing. Always combine the shield with a limit price.

verification.correction: (a) There are no DecryptedExecuted/DecryptedRejected events. pallet_shield emits EncryptedSubmitted{id, who} for submit_encrypted. The store_encrypted path emits ExtrinsicStored/ExtrinsicDispatched/ExtrinsicDispatchFailed/ExtrinsicExpired/ExtrinsicPostponed/ExtrinsicDecodeFailed. Clients find the outcome by locating the inner extrinsic by hash and reading its own success or failure. (b) SDK v10's blocks_for_revealed_execution default is 3, not 5, in v10.0.0, v10.3.2, v10.4.0 and v10.5.0. It is a parameter of mev_submit_encrypted/submit_encrypted_extrinsic, not of add_stake. (c) Hotkey-signed wrappers are not rejected by the chain. Docs say 'The chain accepts a shielded wrapper from any signed origin, but the SDK and CLI refuse to shield hotkey-signed extrinsics as policy'. (d) The 8-block era is enforced by the runtime's CheckMortality wrapper on submit_encrypted (MAX_SHIELD_ERA_PERIOD = 8; longer or immortal eras are rejected as Stale). Everything else is confirmed: ML-KEM-768 + XChaCha20-Poly1305, ciphertext BoundedVec ≤ 8,192 bytes, Shield* timing constants, outer nonce N / inner N+1, v10 BT_MEV_PROTECTION env default, v11 mev_shield on by default for stake intents, the v10.3.2 'Mev Shield Nonce Increment Fix' (#3349), Talisman's single-position inference warning, and PoA. The 'swaps under ~1 TAO gain nothing' claim does not appear in Talisman's doc. Unverified. The mainnet activation date (~2025-12-24) is unverified, though SDK 10.0.0 (2025-12-10) already shipped shield support.
verification.evidence: pallets/shield/src/lib.rs events enum (EncryptedSubmitted, ExtrinsicStored, ExtrinsicDecodeFailed, ExtrinsicDispatchFailed, ExtrinsicDispatched, ExtrinsicExpired, ExtrinsicPostponed, ...). Code index search for DecryptedExecuted/DecryptedRejected returns count 0. runtime/src/check_mortality.rs MAX_SHIELD_ERA_PERIOD = 8. runtime lib.rs ShieldAnnounceAtMs 7,000 / ShieldGraceMs 2,000 / ShieldDecryptWindowMs 3,000. bittensor v10.x core/extrinsics/mev_shield.py: blocks_for_revealed_execution: int = 3. v10.5.0 settings.py DEFAULT_MEV_PROTECTION env check and MAX_MEV_SHIELD_PERIOD = 8. bittensor.com advanced doc MEV section. v10.3.2 release notes.

findings.claim: Keep the coldkey off the bot host and give the bot only a Staking proxy. A leaked Staking proxy still cannot transfer funds out, but it can force value-destroying swaps or moves into thin pools.
findings.detail: Staking proxy allow-list, from the test narrow_proxies_have_exact_allow_lists in runtime/src/proxy_filters/mod.rs: add_collateral, add_stake, add_stake_limit, remove_stake, remove_stake_limit, remove_stake_full_limit, unstake_all, unstake_all_alpha, move_stake, move_stake_limit, set_min_collateral, stake_into_basket, swap_stake, swap_stake_limit. transfer_stake and transfer_stake_and_hotkey are only in Transfer and SmallTransfer (SmallTransfer is strictly below 0.5 TAO / 0.5 alpha). Utility.batch_all is filtered for Staking (CallFiltered), so batched staking needs NonTransfer. NonTransfer excludes balance and stake transfers, coldkey swaps, sudo, EVM, contracts, crowdloan, multisig, basket trading and MevShield::store_encrypted. Deposits: 0.06 TAO + 0.033 TAO per delegation, max 20 proxies; announcements 0.036 + 0.068 TAO, max 75. Delayed proxies need announce, then wait, then execute-proxy-announced (else Unannounced), and the real account can veto. A zero-delay proxy has no veto window, so treat a leaked one as spent. Inferred attack: with only a Staking proxy, an attacker can pre-buy a thin alpha pool and then swap_stake or add_stake the victim's funds into it without a limit, extracting value. Mitigations: keep minimal TAO and stake on the bot's coldkey, use per-strategy coldkeys, and monitor. bt.Policy(max_spend_tao, allowed_netuids, max_fee_tao, allow_raw_calls=False) is client-side only and does not stop a thief who holds the key. Hotkey files under hotkeys/<name> are unencrypted on disk. Coldkey password env vars are BT_WALLET_PASSWORD and BT_WALLET_PASSWORD_FILE. Coldkey swap: announce (36,000-block, about 5-day delay, 0.1 TAO) then swap-coldkey-announced; dispute-coldkey-swap freezes the key.

verification.evidence: The proxy_filters/mod.rs test narrow_proxies_have_exact_allow_lists lists Staking exactly as claimed (14 calls). transfer_stake* appear only in Transfer and SmallTransfer among narrow types. SmallTransfer requires value < SMALL_TRANSFER_LIMIT (500,000,000 rao) and alpha_amount < SMALL_ALPHA_TRANSFER_LIMIT (0.5 alpha) per common/src/lib.rs. tightened_denylist_leaks_stay_denied shows NonTransfer denies swap_coldkey, Sudo::sudo, Multisig::as_multi, Crowdloan::finalize, MevShield::store_encrypted and more.
